title.zh: 卷五十八 列傳第四十八 韋叡 裴邃
title.en: Volume 58 Biographies 48: Wei Rui, Pei Sui
title.raw: 卷五十八 列傳第四十八 韋叡 裴邃 Volume 58 Biographies 48: Wei Rui, Pei Sui

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十八

translations.literal: Biographies 48
translations.idiomatic: the 48th year of Biography

sentences.zh: 韋叡裴邃

translations.literal: Wei Rui, Pei Sui
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rui and Pei Sui

sentences.zh: 叡事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Rui served his stepmother and was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rui was known for the filial devotion he showed his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 祖征累為郡守，每攜叡之職，視之如子。

translations.literal: Zu Zheng repeatedly served as prefectural administrator; each time he took Rui along to his post and regarded him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Zu Zheng held successive prefectships and always took Rui with him on assignment, treating the boy as his own son.

sentences.zh: 時叡內兄王憕、姨弟杜惲並有鄉里盛名，祖征謂叡曰：「汝自謂何如憕、惲？」

translations.literal: At that time Rui's wife's brother Wang Peng and his maternal cousin Du Yun both enjoyed great local renown. Zu Zheng said to Rui, "How do you rate yourself compared with Peng and Yun?
translations.idiomatic: Rui's brother-in-law Wang Peng and his cousin Du Yun were both celebrated in their home district, and Zu Zheng once asked him, "How do you think you measure up to Peng and Yun?

sentences.zh: 叡謙不敢對。

translations.literal: Rui modestly dared not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rui demurred and would not reply.

sentences.zh: 祖征曰：「汝文章或小減，學識當過之。

translations.literal: Zu Zheng said, "Your literary compositions may fall somewhat short, but your learning and understanding ought to surpass theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Zheng said, "Your prose may be a shade weaker, but in breadth of learning you should excel them.

sentences.zh: 然幹國家，成功業，皆莫汝逮也。」

translations.literal: Yet in managing the state and accomplishing great undertakings, none can match you.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to serving the state and achieving great things, however, none of them can equal you.

sentences.zh: 外兄杜幼文為梁州刺史，要叡俱行。

translations.literal: His wife's brother Du Youwen was Governor of Liang Province and invited Rui to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Youwen, another brother-in-law, had been appointed governor of Liang Province and asked Rui to travel with him.

sentences.zh: 梁土富饒，往者多以賄敗，叡雖幼，獨以廉聞。

translations.literal: The Liang region was prosperous and rich; past officials often ruined themselves by bribery. Though Rui was still young, he alone was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a wealthy province and many who served there had been ruined by corruption; though still quite young, Rui alone won a reputation for probity.

sentences.zh: 宋永光初，袁顗為雍州刺史，見而異之，引為主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongguang era of Song, Yuan Yi was Governor of Yong Province; seeing Rui, he was struck by his talent and appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongguang under the Song, Yuan Yi became governor of Yong Province, took an immediate liking to Rui, and made him his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 顗到州，與鄧琬起兵，叡求出為義成郡，故免顗之禍。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the province he rose in arms with Deng Wan; Rui requested assignment as magistrate of Yicheng commandery and thereby escaped Yi's ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi took up his post he joined Deng Wan in rebellion; Rui secured a transfer to Yicheng commandery and so escaped the disaster that befell Yi.

sentences.zh: 累遷齊興太守，本州別駕，長水校尉，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Administrator of Qixing, Senior Assistant of his home province, Colonel of the Chang River, and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts as grand administrator of Qixing, senior assistant of his native province, colonel of the Chang River guard, and general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 齊末多故，欲還鄉里，求為上庸太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi there were many disturbances; wishing to return to his home region, he requested appointment as Grand Administrator of Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qi dynasty collapsed in turmoil he sought to return home and asked to be made grand administrator of Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 俄而太尉陳顯達、護軍將軍崔慧景頻逼建鄴，人心惶駭。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Commandant Chen Xianda and the Protector-General Cui Huijing repeatedly pressed upon Jiankang, and popular sentiment was panic-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Grand Commandant Chen Xianda and Protector-General Cui Huijing were pressing Jiankang again and again, and the capital was gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 西土人謀之，叡曰：「陳雖舊將，非高人才，崔頗更事，懦而不武。

translations.literal: The men of the western regions deliberated with him. Rui said, "Though Chen is an old general, he is no man of towering talent; Cui has seen much service but is timid and not martial.
translations.idiomatic: The western gentry consulted him, and Rui said, "Chen may be a veteran commander, but he lacks true greatness; Cui has experience enough, yet he is timid and no soldier.

sentences.zh: 天下真人，殆興吾州矣。」

translations.literal: The true man of the realm will probably arise in our province.
translations.idiomatic: The man destined to rule the realm will likely rise from our own province.

sentences.zh: 乃遣其二子自結于梁武。

translations.literal: He then sent his two sons to attach themselves to Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly sent his two sons to pledge themselves to Xiao Yan, the future Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及兵起檄至，叡率郡人伐竹為筏，倍道來赴，有眾二千，馬二百匹。

translations.literal: When the army was raised and the proclamation arrived, Rui led the people of his commandery to cut bamboo for rafts, came by forced marches, and had a force of two thousand men and two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the call to arms reached him, he had the people of his commandery cut bamboo for rafts, marched at double speed to join the rising, and brought two thousand men and two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 帝見叡甚悅，撫幾曰：「佗日見君之面，今日見君之心，吾事就矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased to see Rui and, stroking the arm of his seat, said, "Other days I saw your face; today I see your heart—my cause is assured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted to receive him and, patting the arm of his seat, said, "Before I had only seen your face; today I have seen your heart. My enterprise is as good as won.

sentences.zh: 師克郢、魯，平加湖，叡多建策，皆見用。

translations.literal: The army captured Ying and Lu and pacified Jiahu; Rui offered many plans, all of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army took Ying and Lu and pacified Jia Lake, Rui proposed strategy after strategy, and every suggestion was accepted.

sentences.zh: 大軍發郢，謀留守將，上難其人。

translations.literal: The main army set out from Ying; they deliberated on a commander to remain behind, and the Emperor found it hard to choose the man.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force marched out of Ying, they needed a garrison commander, and the emperor could not settle on anyone suitable.

sentences.zh: 久之，顧叡曰：「棄騏驥而不乘，焉遑遑而更索。」

translations.literal: After a long while he turned to Rui and said, "To abandon a thoroughbred and not ride it—why should one hurry about seeking another?
translations.idiomatic: At length he looked at Rui and said, "To leave a thoroughbred unmounted and go frantically searching for another—what sense is there in that?

sentences.zh: 即日以為江夏太守，行郢州府事。

translations.literal: That same day he was made Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and acted in the affairs of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Rui was appointed grand administrator of Jiangxia and entrusted with the civil administration of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 初，郢城之拒守也，男女垂十萬，閉壘經年，疾疫死者十七八，皆積屍於床下，而生者寢處其上，每屋盈滿。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Ying city's stubborn defense, men and women numbered nearly a hundred thousand; the walls were shut for a full year, and seven or eight in ten died of pestilence. Corpses were heaped beneath the beds while the living slept above them, and every house was packed full.
translations.idiomatic: During the long siege of Ying nearly a hundred thousand people had been trapped inside the walls for a year; plague carried off seven or eight in ten, corpses piled under the beds while survivors slept on top of them, and every dwelling was crammed to capacity.

sentences.zh: 叡料簡隱恤，咸為營理，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: Rui assessed and consoled them in secret sympathy, arranging care for all, and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui surveyed their needs with quiet compassion, saw that all were provided for, and the people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，徵為大理。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established he was summoned as Grand Judge.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang regime was founded he was summoned to serve as grand judge.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，遷廷尉，封都梁子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Rui was transferred to Commandant of Justice and enfeoffed as Viscount of Duliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Rui was promoted to commandant of justice and enfeoffed as Viscount of Duliang.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，改封永昌，再遷豫州刺史，領曆陽太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian his fief was changed to Yongchang; he was again transferred to Governor of Yu Province and concurrently Grand Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian his title was changed to Marquis of Yongchang, and he was again made governor of Yu Province while also holding the post of grand administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 魏遣眾來伐，叡率州兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Wei sent a host to attack; Rui led the provincial troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei sent an army against him, Rui led the provincial forces and repulsed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 四年侵魏，詔叡都督眾軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he invaded Wei; an edict appointed Rui commander-in-chief of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian the court launched an invasion of Wei and ordered Rui to command all the forces.

sentences.zh: 叡遣長史王超宗、梁郡太守馮道根攻魏小峴城，未能拔。

translations.literal: Rui sent his chief clerk Wang Chaozong and the Grand Administrator of Liangjun Feng Daogen to attack the Wei fortress of Xiaoxian, but they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent his chief clerk Wang Chaozong and Liang commandery's grand administrator Feng Daogen against the Wei stronghold at Xiaoxian, but they failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 叡巡行圍柵，魏城中忽出數百人陳於門外，叡欲擊之。

translations.literal: Rui was inspecting the siege lines when several hundred men suddenly sallied from the Wei city and formed up outside the gate; Rui wished to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: While Rui was making the rounds of the siege works, several hundred Wei troops suddenly poured out of the city and drew up before the gates; Rui meant to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「向本輕來，請還授甲而後戰。」

translations.literal: The generals all said, "We came out lightly armed just now; let us return, don armor, and then fight.
translations.idiomatic: His officers all urged, "We came out without full armor—let us go back, arm ourselves properly, and then give battle.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「魏城中二千餘人，閉門堅守，足以自保。

translations.literal: Rui said, "In the Wei city there are a little more than two thousand men; shut the gates and hold firm and that is enough to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Rui replied, "There are barely two thousand men in that city; shut the gates and they can hold out well enough on their own.

sentences.zh: 今無故出人於外，必其驍勇，若能挫之，其城自拔。」

translations.literal: Now they have come out for no reason—these must be their fiercest warriors. If we can break them, the city will fall of itself."
translations.idiomatic: To march out for no reason like this means these must be their bravest troops; if we can crush them, the city will surrender without a fight."

sentences.zh: 眾猶遲疑，叡指其節曰：「朝廷授此，非以為飾，韋叡之法，不可犯也。」

translations.literal: The troops still hesitated. Rui pointed to his staff of command and said, "The court bestowed this not as an ornament—Wei Rui's law may not be violated."
translations.idiomatic: The men still wavered, so Rui pointed to his command baton and said, "The court gave me this staff not for show. Wei Rui's orders are not to be disobeyed."

sentences.zh: 乃進兵，魏軍敗，因急攻之，中宿而城拔。

translations.literal: He then advanced; the Wei army was defeated, and pressing the attack hotly, he took the city by midnight.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, routed the Wei force, and pressed the assault so hard that the city fell before midnight.

sentences.zh: 遂進討合肥。

translations.literal: He then marched to attack Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed on against Hefei.

sentences.zh: 先是右軍司馬胡景略至合肥，久未能下，叡案行山川，曰：「吾聞'汾水可以灌平陽'，即此是也。」

translations.literal: Earlier the Right Army Major Hu Jinglue had reached Hefei but long could not reduce it. Rui surveyed the mountains and rivers and said, "I have heard that 'the Fen River can inundate Pingyang'—this is just such a case.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jinglue of the right army staff had already been at Hefei for a long time without success; Rui reconnoitered the terrain and said, "They say the Fen can flood Pingyang—here is our chance to do the same.

sentences.zh: 乃堰肥水。

translations.literal: He then dammed the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly dammed the Fei River.

sentences.zh: 頃之堰成水通，舟艦繼至。

translations.literal: Before long the dam was finished, the water flowed through, and warships arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the dam was complete, the channel filled, and warships began arriving in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 魏初分築東西小城，夾合肥。

translations.literal: Wei had first built separate eastern and western small cities flanking Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had earlier built twin outworks east and west to bracket Hefei.

sentences.zh: 叡先攻二城。

translations.literal: Rui attacked the two cities first.
translations.idiomatic: Rui struck the twin outworks first.

sentences.zh: 既而魏援將楊靈胤帥軍五萬奄至，眾懼不敵，請表益兵。

translations.literal: Then the Wei relief general Yang Lingyin led fifty thousand men in a sudden arrival; the troops feared they could not match them and asked to memorialize for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Wei relief commander Yang Lingyin swept in with fifty thousand men; the army feared it was outmatched and asked to request reinforcements from the throne.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「賊已至城下，方復求軍。

translations.literal: Rui said, "The enemy is already at the walls, and only now you ask for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "The enemy is already at our walls, and only now you want to send for more troops?

sentences.zh: 且吾求濟師，彼亦征眾。

translations.literal: Moreover, if we ask for reinforcements, they too will levy armies.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if we ask for help they will summon still larger hosts in reply.

sentences.zh: '師克在和'，古人之義也。」

translations.literal: "An army conquers through harmony"—that is the ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: "Victory belongs to the army that stands united"—that is what the ancients taught.

sentences.zh: 因戰，破之，軍人少安。

translations.literal: He gave battle and defeated them, and the army's spirits were somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: He gave battle, broke the enemy, and the troops regained their composure.

sentences.zh: 初，肥水堰立，使軍主王懷靜築城於岸守之，魏攻陷城，乘勝至叡堤下。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Fei River dam was built, he had the army commander Wang Huaijing erect a fort on the bank to guard it; Wei attacked and captured the fort, then pressed their advantage to Rui's embankment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fei dam was first raised, Rui had Wang Huaijing build a shore fort to guard it; Wei stormed the fort and, riding their victory, pressed on to Rui's embankment itself.

sentences.zh: 軍監潘靈佑勸叡退還巢湖，諸將又請走保三釜。

translations.literal: The army inspector Pan Lingyou urged Rui to withdraw to Chaohu Lake; the generals again asked to flee and hold Sanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Army inspector Pan Lingyou urged Rui to fall back on Chaohu Lake, and the other commanders again pleaded to retreat and hold the Sanfu line.

sentences.zh: 叡怒曰：「將軍死綏，有前無卻。」

translations.literal: Rui said angrily, "A general dies at his post—advance, never retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Rui flared up and said, "A general dies where he stands—there is only forward, never back.

sentences.zh: 因令取傘扇麾幢樹之堤下，示無動志。

translations.literal: He then ordered umbrellas, fans, banners, and standards taken and planted below the embankment to show he had no thought of moving.
translations.idiomatic: He had parasols, fans, and command banners planted along the embankment to show he had no intention of budging.

sentences.zh: 叡素羸，每戰不嚐騎馬，以板輿自載，督勵眾軍。

translations.literal: Rui had always been frail; in every battle he never rode a horse but was carried in a plank litter, urging and encouraging the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had always been slight of build and never mounted a horse in battle; he was borne in a litter of planks while he drove the army forward.

sentences.zh: 魏兵鑿堤，叡親與爭。

translations.literal: The Wei troops dug at the embankment; Rui personally strove with them over it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei began breaching the dam, Rui joined the struggle in person.

sentences.zh: 魏軍卻，因築壘於堤以自固。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew, and he thereupon built ramparts on the embankment to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei fell back, and he built ramparts atop the embankment to strengthen his position.

sentences.zh: 起鬥艦高與合肥城等，四面臨之。

translations.literal: He raised tower ships as tall as the walls of Hefei and pressed in on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: He raised tower ships level with the walls of Hefei and closed in on the city from every side.

sentences.zh: 城潰，俘獲萬餘，所獲軍實，無所私焉。

translations.literal: The city collapsed; more than ten thousand were captured, and of the military goods taken he kept nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The city gave way; more than ten thousand were taken prisoner, and of the captured stores Rui kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 初，胡景略與前軍趙祖悅同軍交惡，志相陷害，景略一怒，自齧其齒，齒皆流血。

translations.literal: Earlier Hu Jinglue and the vanguard commander Zhao Zuyue, serving in the same army, had become mutually hostile and each sought to harm the other; in a fit of rage Jinglue bit his own teeth until they all bled.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jinglue and the vanguard commander Zhao Zuyue had been at bitter odds within the same army, each plotting against the other; in fury Jinglue once bit his own teeth until the blood ran.

sentences.zh: 叡以將帥不和，將致患禍，酌酒自勸景略曰：「且願兩武勿復私鬥。」

translations.literal: Rui, considering that discord among commanders would bring disaster, poured wine and himself urged Jinglue, saying, "For now let the two warriors cease their private quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: Rui saw that feuding commanders would invite disaster, poured wine, and pressed Jinglue himself: "For now, let the two of you set aside this private feud.

sentences.zh: 故終於此役得無害焉。

translations.literal: Therefore at the end of this campaign no harm came of it.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to that intervention the campaign ended without further harm from their quarrel.

sentences.zh: 叡每晝接客旅，夜算軍書，三更起張燈達曙，撫循其眾，常如不及，故投募之士爭歸之。

translations.literal: Rui each day received travelers and guests; at night he reckoned military documents, rising at the third watch to keep lamps burning until dawn, comforting and guiding his troops as though he could never do enough—therefore men who came to enlist strove to join him.
translations.idiomatic: By day he received visitors; by night he went over dispatches, rising at the third watch and keeping lamps burning until dawn while he tended his men as though he could never do enough—so volunteers flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 所至頓舍修立，館宇藩籬墉壁皆應準繩。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived he set up camps and built structures; lodges, fences, and walls all conformed to the standard measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he halted he laid out camps with disciplined precision—barracks, palisades, and ramparts all built to regulation.

sentences.zh: 合肥既平，有詔班師，去魏軍既近，懼為所躡。

translations.literal: Once Hefei was pacified, an edict ordered withdrawal; the Wei army was close at hand and they feared pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Hefei fell, the court ordered a withdrawal; the Wei were still near, and the army feared pursuit.

sentences.zh: 叡悉遣輜重居前，身乘小輿殿后，魏人服叡威名，望之不敢逼，全軍而還。

translations.literal: Rui sent all baggage and supply trains ahead, himself riding a small litter in the rear guard; the Wei, respecting Rui's martial renown, saw him and dared not press close, and the whole army returned intact.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent all wagons and baggage ahead while he brought up the rear in his litter; the Wei, in awe of his name, dared not close in, and the army returned unscathed.

sentences.zh: 於是遷豫州於合肥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu Province was transferred to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Province was then moved to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏中山王元英攻北徐州，圍刺史昌義之於鍾離，眾兵百萬，連城四十餘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Prince of Zhongshan of Wei, Yuan Ying, attacked Northern Xu Province and besieged the Governor Chang Yizhi at Zhongli; his hosts numbered a million, with more than forty linked fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yuan Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, invaded Northern Xu Province and penned Governor Chang Yizhi inside Zhongli with a host said to number a million men and more than forty fortified camps in a chain.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣征北將軍曹景宗拒之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent the Northern Campaigning General Cao Jingzong to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu dispatched Northern Campaigning General Cao Jingzong to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 次邵陽洲，築壘相守，未敢進。

translations.literal: He halted at Shaoyang Isle, built ramparts, and held his ground without daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao halted at Shaoyang Isle, threw up ramparts, and held his ground without daring to advance.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詔叡會焉，賜以龍環禦刀，曰：「諸將有不用命者斬之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered Rui to join the campaign, bestowing on him the imperial dragon-ring saber and saying, "Any general who disobeys shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Rui to join the relief force, giving him the imperial dragon-ring saber with the words, "Behead any commander who fails to obey.

sentences.zh: 叡自合肥徑陰陵大澤，過澗穀，輒飛橋以濟師。

translations.literal: Rui from Hefei went straight through the great marshes of Yinling; wherever he crossed streams and ravines he at once threw flying bridges to get the army across.
translations.idiomatic: Rui marched from Hefei straight through the Yinling marshes; wherever streams and ravines blocked the way he threw flying bridges across to keep the army moving.

sentences.zh: 人畏魏軍盛，多勸叡緩行。

translations.literal: Men feared the Wei army's strength and many urged Rui to march slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Many feared the size of the Wei host and urged Rui to slow his march.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「鍾離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎。」

translations.literal: Rui said, "At Zhongli they now dwell in burrowed caves, drawing water with their backs to the doorposts; chariots race and soldiers run yet still fear they come too late—how much more if we go slowly?
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "At Zhongli they are living in burrows and hauling water with their backs to the doorposts; even chariots at full gallop and men at the run may arrive too late—how then can we afford to dawdle?

sentences.zh: 旬日而至邵陽。

translations.literal: Within ten days he reached Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he reached Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，帝敕景宗曰：「韋叡卿鄉望，宜善敬之。」

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had charged Jingzong, saying, "Wei Rui is a man of standing in your home district—you should treat him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already instructed Cao Jingzong, "Wei Rui is a man of standing in your own district—treat him with respect.

sentences.zh: 景宗見叡甚謹。

translations.literal: Jingzong received Rui with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Cao received him with marked deference.

sentences.zh: 帝聞曰：「二將和，師必濟矣。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he said, "The two generals are in harmony—the army is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he said, "With those two generals in accord, the army is bound to prevail.

sentences.zh: 叡于景宗營前二十里，夜掘長塹，樹鹿角，截洲為城，比曉而營立。

translations.literal: Rui encamped twenty li before Jingzong's position; by night he dug a long trench, planted chevaux-de-frise, and cut off the isle to make a walled camp—by dawn the fortifications stood complete.
translations.idiomatic: Rui pitched camp twenty li in front of Cao's lines; that night he dug a long trench, set chevaux-de-frise, and walled off the isle into a fortified camp that stood complete by dawn.

sentences.zh: 元英大驚，以杖擊地曰：「是何神也！」

translations.literal: Yuan Ying was greatly startled and struck the ground with his staff, saying, "What sort of spirits are these!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying was thunderstruck and struck the ground with his staff, crying, "What manner of sorcery is this!

sentences.zh: 景宗慮城中危懼，乃募軍士言文達、洪騏驎等齎敕入城，使固城守，潛行水底，得達東城。

translations.literal: Jingzong, fearing panic in the city, then recruited the soldiers Yan Wenda and Hong Qilin and others to carry the imperial edict into the city and strengthen its defense; traveling underwater in secret they reached the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic inside Zhongli, Cao recruited soldiers Yan Wenda and Hong Qilin to carry the imperial edict into the city by swimming underwater and reached the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 城中戰守日苦，始知有援，於是人百其勇。

translations.literal: Inside the city the hardships of battle and defense grew daily; only then did they learn relief had come, and thereafter every man fought with redoubled courage.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders had been growing daily more desperate; once they knew relief had come, every man fought as if he were a hundred.

sentences.zh: 魏將楊大眼將萬餘騎來戰，大眼以勇冠三軍，所向皆靡。

translations.literal: The Wei general Yang Dayan led more than ten thousand horsemen to give battle; Dayan's courage was foremost in the whole army and wherever he went all were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei commander Yang Dayan came to fight with more than ten thousand cavalry; famed as the bravest man in the army, he swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 叡結車為陣，大眼聚騎圍之。

translations.literal: Rui formed wagons into a battle line; Dayan massed his cavalry and surrounded them.
translations.idiomatic: Rui drew up his wagons in battle formation; Dayan massed his horsemen and encircled them.

sentences.zh: 叡以強弩二千一時俱發，洞甲穿中，殺傷者眾。

translations.literal: Rui had two thousand powerful crossbows fire all at once; they pierced armor through and through, and the killed and wounded were many.
translations.idiomatic: Rui loosed two thousand heavy crossbows at once; bolts pierced clean through armor, and casualties piled up on every side.

sentences.zh: 矢貫大眼右臂，亡魂而走。

translations.literal: An arrow transfixed Dayan's right arm and he fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt drove through Dayan's right arm and he fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 明旦，元英自率眾來戰，叡乘素木輿，執白角如意以麾軍，一日數合，英甚憚其強。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Yuan Ying personally led his troops to battle; Rui rode in a plain wooden litter, holding a white-horn ruyi scepter to command the army—several engagements in a single day—and Ying greatly feared his strength.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yuan Ying led the assault in person; Rui sat in a plain wooden litter, directing the army with a white-horn ruyi scepter, and fought several engagements in one day until Ying came to dread his force.

sentences.zh: 魏軍又夜來攻城，飛矢雨集。

translations.literal: The Wei army again came by night to assault the walls; flying arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei attacked again by night, and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 叡子黯請下城以避箭，叡不許。

translations.literal: Rui's son An asked to leave the wall to avoid the arrows; Rui would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's son An begged to leave the wall to escape the arrows; Rui refused.

sentences.zh: 軍中驚，叡於城上厲聲呵之乃定。

translations.literal: The army was alarmed; Rui on the wall shouted them down in a stern voice and only then were they steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the ranks until Rui shouted them down from the wall in a voice of iron and restored order.

sentences.zh: 魏人先于邵陽洲兩岸為兩橋，樹柵數百步，跨淮通道。

translations.literal: The Wei had first built two bridges on both banks of Shaoyang Isle, planting palisades for several hundred paces to span the Huai and open a passage.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei had already thrown two bridges across Shaoyang Isle with palisaded approaches hundreds of paces long to carry the Huai crossing.

sentences.zh: 叡裝大艦，使梁郡太守馮道根、廬江太守裴邃、秦郡太守李文釗等為水軍。

translations.literal: Rui fitted out great warships and appointed the Grand Administrators Feng Daogen of Liangjun, Pei Sui of Lujiang, and Li Wenzhao of Qin commandery and others as the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Rui fitted out heavy warships and placed Liang's Feng Daogen, Lujiang's Pei Sui, Qin's Li Wenzhao, and others in command of the fleet.

sentences.zh: 會淮水暴長，叡即遣之，鬥艦競發，皆臨賊壘。

translations.literal: It happened that the Huai River rose violently; Rui at once sent them forth, tower ships racing to launch, all pressing upon the enemy ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai suddenly swelled in flood; Rui launched the fleet at once, tower ships racing forward to bear down on the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 以小船載草，灌之以膏，從而焚其橋。

translations.literal: Small boats loaded with straw were soaked in grease and sent to burn their bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Small boats packed with straw and soaked in oil were sent to set the bridges ablaze.

sentences.zh: 風怒火盛，敢死之士拔柵斫橋，水又漂疾，倏忽之間，橋柵盡壞。

translations.literal: Wind fanned the raging flames; dare-to-die men tore up the palisades and hacked at the bridges, while the water surged swift as well—in an instant bridges and palisades were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wind drove the flames higher; suicide squads tore down palisades and hacked at the bridges while the current raced—within moments bridges and stockades were gone.

sentences.zh: 道根等皆身自搏戰，軍人奮勇，呼聲動天地，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Feng Daogen and the others all fought in person; the soldiers fought with fierce courage, their shouts shaking heaven and earth, and not one failed to match a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen and the rest fought hand to hand; the soldiers' battle cries shook heaven and earth, and each man fought as if he were a hundred.

sentences.zh: 魏人大潰，元英脫身遁走。

translations.literal: The Wei army collapsed in great rout; Yuan Ying slipped away and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army broke in utter rout, and Yuan Ying escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 魏軍趨水死者十餘萬，斬首亦如之，其餘釋甲稽顙乞為囚奴猶數十萬。

translations.literal: Wei troops who rushed into the water and drowned numbered more than a hundred thousand; heads cut off were as many, and the rest who cast off armor and knocked their foreheads begging to be prisoners still numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand Wei soldiers drowned rushing for the water; heads taken in battle matched that toll, and still hundreds of thousands threw down their armor and kowtowed to beg for mercy.

sentences.zh: 叡遣報昌義之，義之且悲且喜，不暇答，但叫曰：「更生！

translations.literal: Rui sent word to report to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi, both grieving and rejoicing, had no leisure to reply but only cried out, "Reborn!
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent word to Chang Yizhi, who was too overcome with grief and joy to answer and could only cry, "Reborn!

sentences.zh: 更生！」

translations.literal: Reborn!
translations.idiomatic: Reborn!

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書郎周舍勞軍於淮上。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the Secretariat Gentleman Zhou She to comfort the army on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Secretariat Gentleman Zhou She to congratulate the army on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 叡積所獲於軍門，舍觀之，謂叡曰：「君此獲復與熊耳山等矣。」

translations.literal: Rui piled up what had been captured before the army gate; Zhou She came to view it and said to Rui, "With this haul you have again equaled Bear's-Ear Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Rui stacked the captured booty before the army gate; Zhou She came to inspect it and told Rui, "With spoils like these you have matched your feat at Bear's-Ear Mountain once more.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For his merit his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement his rank was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷左衛將軍，俄為安西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to General of the Left Guard; soon after he became Western Pacification Chief Clerk and Grand Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made general of the left guard, and soon afterward became chief clerk of the western pacification command and grand administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 會司州刺史馬仙琕自北還軍，為魏人所躡，三關擾動。

translations.literal: It happened that the Governor of Si Province Ma Xiàn was returning from the north with his army and was pursued by Wei; the three passes were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: About that time Governor Ma Xiàn of Si Province was returning from the north with his army when Wei forces gave chase and threw the three frontier passes into alarm.

sentences.zh: 詔叡督眾軍援焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rui to command all armies in relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Rui to take command of all relief forces.

sentences.zh: 叡至安陸，增築城二丈餘，更開大塹，起高樓。

translations.literal: Rui reached Anlu, raised the city walls more than two zhang, opened a great moat anew, and erected tall towers.
translations.idiomatic: Rui reached Anlu, raised the city walls more than two zhang, dug a new deep moat, and built tall watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 眾頗譏其示弱，叡曰：「不然，為將當有怯時。」

translations.literal: The troops largely mocked this as showing weakness; Rui said, "Not so—a general must have timid moments.
translations.idiomatic: Many troops mocked this as a show of weakness, but Rui said, "Not at all—a good general must know when to be cautious.

sentences.zh: 是時，元英復追仙琕，將復邵陽之恥，聞叡至乃退，帝亦詔罷軍。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Ying was again pursuing Xiàn, intending to wipe away the shame of Shaoyang; hearing Rui had arrived he withdrew, and the Emperor also ordered the armies disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying was again pursuing Ma Xiàn, intent on avenging the defeat at Shaoyang; when he heard Rui had arrived he withdrew, and the emperor also ordered the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為丹陽尹，以公事免。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he became Intendant of Danyang and was dismissed on official business.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became intendant of Danyang but was dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 初，叡起兵鄉中，客陰雙光泣止叡，叡還為州，雙光道候。

translations.literal: Earlier when Rui raised troops in his home district, his guest Yin Shuangguang wept and tried to stop him; when Rui returned as governor, Shuangguang came to the road to greet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui first raised troops in his home district, his friend Yin Shuangguang had wept and begged him to desist; now, returning as governor, Rui found Shuangguang waiting on the road to greet him.

sentences.zh: 叡笑曰：「若從公言，乞食于路矣。」

translations.literal: Rui laughed and said, "Had I followed your advice I would be begging along the road today.
translations.idiomatic: Rui laughed and said, "Had I taken your advice, I would be begging along the roadside today.

sentences.zh: 餉耕牛十頭。

translations.literal: He presented him with ten plow oxen.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him ten plow oxen as a gift.

sentences.zh: 叡於故舊無所惜，士大夫年七十以上，多與假板縣令，鄉里甚懷之。

translations.literal: Rui was unstinting toward old friends; for gentry over seventy he often provisionally granted the post of county magistrate, and the countryside cherished him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was generous to the point of extravagance with old friends; for scholars over seventy he often granted provisional appointment as county magistrate, and the countryside held him in deep affection.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜表致仕，優詔不許。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he memorialized to retire; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, but a gracious edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 徵拜護軍，給鼓吹一部，入直殿省。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Protector of the Army, granted one set of martial music, and entered attendance in the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as protector of the army, granted a military band, and took up duty in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 居朝廷恂恂，未嘗忤視，武帝甚禮敬之。

translations.literal: In court he was deferential and never met the emperor's gaze improperly; Emperor Wu treated him with great courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: In court he was humble and respectful, never meeting the emperor's gaze improperly, and Emperor Wu treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 性慈愛，撫孤兄子過於己子，曆官所得祿賜，皆散之親故，家無餘財。

translations.literal: By nature loving and kind, he reared his orphaned nephews more attentively than his own sons; salaries and gifts from every office he distributed among kin and friends, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Kind by nature, he cared for his orphaned nephews more devotedly than for his own sons; every salary and gift from office he distributed among relatives and friends, leaving nothing in the house.

sentences.zh: 後為護軍，居家無事，慕萬石、陸賈之為人，因畫之於壁以自玩。

translations.literal: Later as Protector of the Army, idle at home, he admired the conduct of the Wanshi family and Lu Jia and had them painted on his walls for his own delight.
translations.idiomatic: Later, idle at home as protector of the army, he admired the Wanshi family and Lu Jia and had portraits of them painted on his walls for his own enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 時雖老，暇日猶課諸兒以學。

translations.literal: Though old by then, on free days he still drilled his sons in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, he still set his sons lessons on his free days.

sentences.zh: 第三子棱尤明經史，世稱其洽聞。

translations.literal: His third son Leng was especially versed in the classics and histories; the age praised his wide learning.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Leng was especially learned in the classics and histories, and the age praised his encyclopedic knowledge.

sentences.zh: 叡每坐使棱說書，其所發擿，棱猶弗之逮。

translations.literal: Rui each time he sat had Leng expound texts; the points Leng raised Rui still could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Rui sat for discussion he had Leng expound the texts, yet the points Leng raised still fell short of what Rui himself could draw out.

sentences.zh: 武帝方銳意釋氏，天下咸從風而化。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was then intent on Buddhism and all under heaven followed the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was then wholly devoted to Buddhism, and all under heaven followed suit.

sentences.zh: 叡自以信受素薄，位居大臣，不欲與眾俯仰，所行略如佗日。

translations.literal: Rui considered his own faith shallow and, holding high ministerial rank, did not wish to bow with the multitude; his conduct remained much as before.
translations.idiomatic: Rui felt his own Buddhist devotion had always been shallow; as a senior minister he did not wish to bow with the crowd, and his conduct remained much as it had always been.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，遷侍中、車騎將車，未拜，卒於家，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he was transferred to Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry but before assuming office died at home, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he was promoted to palace attendant and general of chariots and cavalry, but before he could take up the post he died at home at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: His final testament ordered a simple burial, enshrouded in daily dress.
translations.idiomatic: His testament ordered a plain burial in everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 武帝即日臨器甚慟，贈車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰嚴。

translations.literal: That same day Emperor Wu came to the bier and grieved greatly, posthumously granting General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Marshal with orders equal to the Three Dukes; his posthumous title was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Emperor Wu came to the bier in deep grief, posthumously granting him general of chariots and cavalry and grand marshal with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous name was Yan.

sentences.zh: 叡雅有曠世之度，蒞人以愛惠為本，所居必有政績。

translations.literal: Rui possessed in elegant measure a transcendental breadth; governing men he took loving kindness as root, and wherever he served there were administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Rui possessed a rare breadth of spirit; he governed through kindness and compassion, and wherever he served he left a record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 將兵仁愛，士卒營幕未立，終不肯舍，井灶未成，亦不先食。

translations.literal: Leading troops he was benevolent: until the soldiers' camps and tents were pitched he would not lodge, and until wells and kitchens were done he would not eat first.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he was humane: he would not retire until his men's tents were pitched, and would not eat until their wells and kitchens were ready.

sentences.zh: 被服必於儒者，雖臨陣交鋒，常緩服乘輿，執竹如意以麾進止，與裴邃俱為梁世名將，余人莫及。

translations.literal: His attire was always that of a scholar; even when crossing spears in battle he commonly wore loose robes in a litter, holding a bamboo ruyi to direct advance and halt—he and Pei Sui together were famed generals of the Liang age, and others could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: He always dressed as a scholar; even in the heat of battle he wore loose robes in a litter and directed movements with a bamboo ruyi scepter. He and Pei Sui were the Liang dynasty's greatest generals, and none could equal them.

sentences.zh: 初，邵陽之役，昌義之甚德叡，請曹景宗與叡會，因設錢二十萬官賭之。

translations.literal: Earlier at the Shaoyang campaign Chang Yizhi owed Rui deep gratitude and asked Cao Jingzong to meet with Rui; they thereupon staked an official wager of two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle at Shaoyang, Chang Yizhi was deeply grateful to Rui and arranged a meeting with Cao Jingzong; the three of them wagered two hundred thousand cash in an official game.

sentences.zh: 景宗擲得雉，叡徐擲得盧，遽取一子反之，曰：「異事」，遂作塞。

translations.literal: Jingzong threw and got a pheasant; Rui slowly threw and got a deer, then quickly took one piece and turned it over, saying "Strange," and thus made a blockade win.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong threw and scored a pheasant; Rui threw slowly and scored a deer, then swiftly flipped a piece and cried, "How strange!"—winning with a blockade.

sentences.zh: 景宗時與群帥爭先啟之捷，叡獨居後，其不尚勝率多如是，世尤以此賢之。

translations.literal: Jingzong then vied with the other commanders to be first in reporting victory; Rui alone held back—his disdain for triumph was mostly thus, and the age especially prized him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was then racing the other commanders to be first in reporting victory, while Rui alone held back; his reluctance to claim credit was typical, and the age especially admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 叡兄纂、闡，並早知名。

translations.literal: Rui's elder brothers Zuan and Chan were both early known.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's elder brothers Zuan and Chan had both been famous early on.

sentences.zh: 纂仕齊位司徒記室、特進，沈約嘗稱纂於上曰：「恨陛下不與此人同時，其學非臣輩也。」

translations.literal: Zuan served Qi as Secretariat of the Grand Mentor and Special Advance; Shen Yue once praised Zuan to the throne, saying, "I regret Your Majesty was not contemporary with this man—his learning is not of our sort.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had served the Qi as secretariat of the grand mentor and special advance; Shen Yue once told the emperor, "I regret Your Majesty was not born in the same age as this man—his learning is beyond anything we can match.

sentences.zh: 闡為建寧縣，所得俸祿百餘萬，還家悉委伯父處分，鄉里宗事之。

translations.literal: Chan was magistrate of Jianning; his salary and emoluments amounted to more than a million, and returning home he handed all to his paternal uncle for disposal—the village regarded him with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Chan served as magistrate of Jianning; his salary and emoluments totaled more than a million cash, and on returning home he handed everything to his uncle for disposal—the village honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 位通直郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Direct Communication Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of direct communication gentleman.

sentences.zh: 叡子放字元直，身長七尺七寸，腰帶八圍，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: Rui's son Fang, style Yuanchi, stood seven feet seven inches, his belt eight spans round, and his bearing very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's son Fang, courtesy name Yuanchi, stood seven feet seven inches tall with an eight-span waist and a strikingly imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 襲封永昌縣侯，位竟陵太守。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Yongchang county and held the post of Grand Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate of Yongchang county and served as grand administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 在郡和理，為吏人所稱。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was harmonious and orderly, praised by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was fair and orderly, winning praise from officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，徙北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was moved to Governor of Northern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to governor of Northern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮，諡曰宜侯。

translations.literal: He died in his post; his posthumous title was Marquis Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post; his posthumous title was Marquis Yi.

sentences.zh: 放性弘厚篤實，輕財好施，于諸弟尤雍穆。

translations.literal: Fang's nature was magnanimous, sincere, and solid; he lightly regarded wealth and loved to give, and among his brothers was especially harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was magnanimous, sincere, and steadfast; he cared little for wealth and loved to give, and was especially close with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 每將遠別及行役初還，常同一室臥起，時比之三薑。

translations.literal: Whenever about to part on a distant journey or just returned from service, they commonly slept and rose in one room, and the times compared them to the three Jiang brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they faced a long separation or had just returned from service, they slept and rose in the same room; people compared them to the three Jiang brothers of old.

sentences.zh: 初，放與吳郡張率皆有側室懷孕，因指為昏姻。

translations.literal: Earlier Fang and Zhang Shuai of Wu commandery both had concubines pregnant, and they pointed to this as a betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fang and Zhang Shuai of Wu commandery each had a concubine who was pregnant, and they agreed this meant their children should marry.

sentences.zh: 其後各產男女，未及成長而率亡，遺嗣孤弱，放常贈恤之。

translations.literal: Later each bore sons and daughters; before they grew up Shuai died, leaving orphaned heirs weak, and Fang often sent gifts and relief.
translations.idiomatic: Each later had children, but before they came of age Shuai died, leaving orphaned heirs; Fang often sent them gifts and support.

sentences.zh: 及為北徐州，時有貴族請昏者，放曰：「吾不失信于故友。」

translations.literal: When he was in Northern Xu a noble family requested marriage; Fang said, "I will not break faith with an old friend.
translations.idiomatic: When he was governor of Northern Xu a noble family sought a marriage alliance, but Fang said, "I will not break faith with an old friend.

sentences.zh: 及以息岐娶率女，又以女適率子，時稱放能篤舊。

translations.literal: He then had his son Qi marry Shuai's daughter and gave his own daughter to Shuai's son; the age praised Fang for steadfast loyalty to old ties.
translations.idiomatic: He had his son Qi marry Shuai's daughter and gave his own daughter to Shuai's son; the age praised Fang for his loyalty to old friendships.

sentences.zh: 子粲。

translations.literal: His son Can.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Can.

sentences.zh: 粲字長倩，少有父風，好學仗氣，身長八尺，容觀甚偉。

translations.literal: Can, style Changqian, in youth had his father's manner, loved learning and bore himself with spirit, stood eight feet, and his appearance was imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Can, courtesy name Changqian, had his father's bearing from youth; he loved learning and carried himself with spirit, stood eight feet tall, and had a commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 初為雲麾晉安王行參軍，後為外兵參軍兼中兵。

translations.literal: He first served as Mobile Corps Aide to the Prince of Jin'an of the Cloud-Banner guard, later as External Troops Aide while also holding Central Troops Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He began as aide-de-camp to the Prince of Jin'an of the Cloud-Banner guard, then served as external troops aide while also holding the central troops post.

sentences.zh: 時潁川庾仲容、吳郡張率前輩才名，與粲同府，並忘年交好。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Zhongrong of Yingchuan and Zhang Shuai of Wu commandery were senior men of talent and fame; they served in the same office as Can and all became friends across the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongrong of Yingchuan and Zhang Shuai of Wu were celebrated senior talents who served in the same office; all three became close friends despite the age gap.

sentences.zh: 及王為皇太子，粲自記室遷步兵校尉，入為東宮領直，後襲爵永昌縣侯，累遷左衛率，領直。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Can moved from secretariat to Colonel of Footsoldiers, entered as Eastern Palace Duty Officer, later inherited the marquisate of Yongchang county, and was promoted in succession to Left Guard Commander while retaining duty officer status.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Can rose from secretariat to colonel of footsoldiers and entered the eastern palace as duty officer; he later inherited the marquisate of Yongchang and was promoted to commander of the left guard while retaining his duty post.

sentences.zh: 粲以舊恩，任寄綢密，雖居職累徙，常留宿衛。

translations.literal: Because of old favor Can's trust and commission were intimate; though his offices changed repeatedly, he was constantly kept on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his long-standing favor with the crown prince, Can enjoyed the prince's intimate trust; though his titles changed often, he was always kept on palace night guard.

sentences.zh: 頗擅權誕倨，不為時輩所平。

translations.literal: He rather monopolized power and was arrogant; his contemporaries did not approve of him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew arrogant with power and was disliked by his peers.

sentences.zh: 右衛朱異嘗于酒席厲色謂粲曰：「卿何得已作領軍面向人！」

translations.literal: Zhu Yi of the Right Guard once at a banquet said sternly to Can, "How dare you already act like a commander-in-chief before people!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi of the right guard once said sharply to Can at a banquet, "Who do you think you are, acting like commander-in-chief already?

sentences.zh: 大同中，帝嘗不豫，一日暴劇，皇太子以下併入侍疾，內外咸雲帝崩。

translations.literal: In Datong the Emperor once fell ill; one day his condition turned suddenly severe, and from the crown prince down all entered to attend his sickness—inside and outside all said the Emperor had died.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong the emperor fell ill; one day his condition suddenly worsened, and everyone from the crown prince down rushed to his bedside; inside and outside the palace, all believed the emperor had died.

sentences.zh: 粲將率宮甲度台，微有喜色，問所由那不見辦長梯。

translations.literal: Can was about to lead palace armor across the terrace with a slight look of joy, asking the road-master why the long ladder had not been prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Can was preparing to lead palace guards across the terrace with a faint look of satisfaction, asking why the long ladder had not been readied.

sentences.zh: 以為大行幸前殿，須長梯以復也。

translations.literal: He thought the late emperor would proceed to the front hall and a long ladder would be needed for the ascent.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed the deceased emperor would be carried to the front hall and a long ladder would be needed for the bier.

sentences.zh: 帝后聞之，怒曰：「韋粲願我死。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor and Empress heard of it they said angrily, "Wei Can wishes me dead.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress heard of this they said angrily, "Wei Can wants me dead.

sentences.zh: 有司奏推之，帝曰：「各為其主，不足推。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized to prosecute him; the Emperor said, "Each serves his lord—no need to prosecute."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities memorialized for his prosecution, but the emperor said, "He was only serving his master—let it pass."

sentences.zh: 故出為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Therefore he was sent out as Governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly sent out as governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出餞新亭，執粲手曰：「與卿不為久別。」

translations.literal: The crown prince came out to Xinting to see him off, took Can's hand and said, "This parting with you will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince saw him off at Xinting, took his hand, and said, "We will not be apart for long.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝復召還為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After a long while the Emperor again summoned him back as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor recalled him as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 還至廬陵，聞侯景作逆，便簡閱部下，倍道赴援。

translations.literal: Returning to Luling he heard Hou Jing had rebelled; he at once inspected his subordinates and came by forced marches to aid.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Luling he heard that Hou Jing had rebelled; he immediately mustered his troops and marched at double speed to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 至豫章，即就內史劉孝儀共謀之。

translations.literal: Reaching Yuzhang he at once went to the Interior Minister Liu Xiaoyi to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yuzhang he went straight to Interior Minister Liu Xiaoyi to consult with him.

sentences.zh: 孝儀曰：「必如此，當有敕，安可輕信單使，妄相驚動。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi said, "If it were truly so there would be an edict—how can one lightly trust a lone messenger and rashly stir alarm?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi said, "If that were true there would be an imperial edict—how can we lightly trust a lone messenger and stir up panic for nothing?

sentences.zh: 或恐不然。」

translations.literal: Perhaps it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: It may well be untrue.

sentences.zh: 時孝儀置酒，粲怒以杯抵地曰：「賊已度江，便逼宮闕，水陸阻斷，何暇有報；

translations.literal: At that time Xiaoyi was setting out wine; Can angrily struck the cup to the ground and said, "The rebels have already crossed the river and press upon the palace gates; land and water routes are cut—where is there time for reports?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was hosting a banquet; Can slammed his cup to the floor and said, "The rebels have crossed the Yangzi and are pressing on the palace—communications are cut on land and water; who has time to wait for edicts?

sentences.zh: 假令無敕，豈得自安。

translations.literal: Even if there were no edict, how could one rest secure?
translations.idiomatic: Even without an edict, how can we sit idle in safety?

sentences.zh: 韋粲今日何情飲酒。」

translations.literal: What mood has Wei Can today for drinking wine?"
translations.idiomatic: What business has Wei Can drinking wine today?"

sentences.zh: 即馳馬出，部分將發。

translations.literal: He at once galloped out and arrayed his forces to set forth.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped out at once and began deploying his troops for the march.

sentences.zh: 會江州刺史當陽公大心遣使要粲，粲乃分麾下配第八弟助、第九弟警為前軍。

translations.literal: It happened that the Governor of Jiang Province, the Duke of Dangyang Daxin, sent a messenger to summon Can; Can then divided his command, assigning his eighth brother Zhu and ninth brother Jing as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Jiang Province, Duke Daxin of Dangyang, sent to summon him; Can divided his forces and placed his eighth brother Zhu and ninth brother Jing in command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 粲馳往見大心曰：「上游蕃鎮，江州去都最近，殿下情計，實宜在先。

translations.literal: Can galloped to see Daxin and said, "The frontier strongholds of the upper reaches—Jiang Province is nearest the capital; Your Highness's intent and plan ought truly to come first.
translations.idiomatic: Can rode to see Daxin and said, "Among the upper Yangzi garrisons, Jiang Province is closest to the capital—Your Highness ought to take the lead in this crisis.

sentences.zh: 但中流任重，當須應接，不可闕鎮。

translations.literal: But the midstream bears heavy responsibility and must be held in support; the garrison cannot be left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: But the mid-Yangzi sector is critical and must be held—you cannot leave the province unguarded.

sentences.zh: 今宜張軍聲勢，移鎮盆城，遣偏將賜隨，於事便足。」

translations.literal: Now you should display military might, shift your headquarters to Pencheng, and send a subordinate general to accompany us—that will suffice for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: You should make a show of force, move your headquarters to Pencheng, and send a subordinate commander with us—that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 大心然之，遣中兵柳昕帥兵二千隨粲。

translations.literal: Daxin agreed and sent Central Troops Commander Liu Xin leading two thousand men to follow Can.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin agreed and sent Liu Xin with two thousand men to accompany Can.

sentences.zh: 粲悉留家累于江州，以輕舸就路。

translations.literal: Can left all his family dependents in Jiang Province and set out in light boats.
translations.idiomatic: Can left his entire family in Jiang Province and set out in light boats.

sentences.zh: 至南洲，粲外弟司州刺史柳仲禮亦帥步騎萬餘人至橫江。

translations.literal: Reaching Nan Isle, Can's wife's brother the Governor of Si Province Liu Zhongli also led more than ten thousand foot and horse to Hengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Nan Isle his cousin Liu Zhongli, governor of Si Province, also arrived at Hengjiang with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 粲即送糧仗給之，並散私金帛以賞其戰士。

translations.literal: Can at once sent grain and weapons to supply him and also distributed his private gold and silks to reward the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Can immediately sent him grain and arms and distributed his own gold and silks to reward Zhongli's soldiers.

sentences.zh: 先是，安北鄱陽王範亦自合肥遣西豫州刺史裴之高與其世子嗣帥江西之眾赴都，屯于張公洲，待上流諸軍。

translations.literal: Earlier the Northern Pacification Prince of Poyang Fan had also from Hefei sent the Governor of Western Yu Pei Zhigao and his heir Si leading the hosts of the western river region to the capital, encamped at Zhanggong Isle, awaiting the upper-stream armies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Fan of Poyang, northern pacification commander, had sent Western Yu governor Pei Zhigao and his heir Si from Hefei with the Jiangxi forces toward the capital, encamped at Zhanggong Isle to await the upper Yangzi armies.

sentences.zh: 至是，之高遣船度仲禮，與粲合軍進屯新林王游苑。

translations.literal: At this time Zhigao sent boats to ferry Zhongli across; he joined forces with Can and advanced to encamp at the Xinglin Royal Pleasure Park.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao now sent boats to ferry Zhongli across; he and Can united their forces and encamped at the Xinglin Royal Park.

sentences.zh: 粲建議推仲禮為大都督，報下流眾軍。

translations.literal: Can proposed promoting Zhongli as supreme commander and reported this to the armies of the lower reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Can proposed making Zhongli supreme commander and notified the downstream forces.

sentences.zh: 裴之高自以年位高，恥居其下。

translations.literal: Pei Zhigao considered himself senior in years and rank and was ashamed to stand beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhigao, considering himself senior in age and rank, was ashamed to serve under Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 乃云：「柳節下已是州將，何須我復鞭板。」

translations.literal: He then said, "Master Liu is already a provincial commander—why need I again crack the whip and board?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Master Liu is already a provincial commander—why should I still play the subordinate?

sentences.zh: 累日不決。

translations.literal: For many days no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: For days no agreement could be reached.

sentences.zh: 粲乃抗言於眾曰：「今同赴國難，義在除賊，所以推柳司州者，政以久捍邊疆，先為侯景所憚。

translations.literal: Can then spoke boldly before the assembly, saying, "Today we together face the state's peril; righteousness lies in destroying the rebels. The reason for promoting Governor Liu of Si is precisely that he long defended the frontier and was already feared by Hou Jing first.
translations.idiomatic: Can then addressed the assembly boldly: "We share a national crisis and our duty is to destroy the rebels. I propose Liu of Si because he has long defended the frontier and Hou Jing already fears him.

sentences.zh: 且士馬精銳，無出其前。

translations.literal: Moreover his troops and horses are elite and sharp—none surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: His troops are the finest in the field—none can match them.

sentences.zh: 若論位次，柳在粲下，語其年齒，亦少於粲，直以社稷之計，不得復論。

translations.literal: If one speaks of rank, Liu stands below Can; speaking of age, he is also younger than Can—only for the sake of the altars of state can we no longer argue.
translations.idiomatic: By rank Liu stands below me, and by age he is younger—but for the sake of the realm we cannot argue over precedence.

sentences.zh: 今日貴在將和，若人心不同，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Today what is precious is harmony among generals; if hearts are not united the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Today unity among commanders is what matters; if we are divided, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 裴公朝之舊齒，豈應復挾私以阻大計。

translations.literal: Lord Pei is an old pillar of the court—how should he again harbor private feelings to obstruct the great plan?
translations.idiomatic: Lord Pei is a veteran of the court—surely he will not let private pride block the common cause.

sentences.zh: 粲請為諸君解釋之。」

translations.literal: Can asks to explain this for you all.
translations.idiomatic: Let me go and explain this to him on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 乃單舸至之高營切讓之。

translations.literal: He then went alone in a small boat to Zhigao's camp and sternly reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: He took a single boat to Zhigao's camp and spoke to him sharply.

sentences.zh: 之高泣曰：「吾荷國榮，自應帥先士卒，顧恨衰老，不能效命，企望柳使君共平凶逆。

translations.literal: Zhigao wept and said, "I have received the state's honor and ought myself to lead the soldiers in the van; I only regret my old age and cannot devote my life, and look to Master Liu to together pacify the villainous rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao wept and said, "I owe the state a debt of honor and ought to lead the charge myself; but I am old and cannot serve as I once did, and I place my hopes in Master Liu to crush the rebels together.

sentences.zh: 前謂眾議已定，無俟老夫爾。

translations.literal: Earlier I thought the assembly's deliberation was settled and there was no need to wait for this old man.
translations.idiomatic: I thought the matter was already settled and had no need of an old man like me.

sentences.zh: 若必有疑，當剖心相示。」

translations.literal: If there must still be doubt, I should lay open my heart to show it.
translations.idiomatic: If there is still doubt, I will lay open my heart to prove my sincerity.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將定議，仲禮方得進軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals settled their deliberation and Zhongli was finally able to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders then reached agreement, and Zhongli was able to advance.

sentences.zh: 次新亭，賊列陣于中興寺，相持至晚各解歸。

translations.literal: They next halted at Xinting; the rebels formed battle lines at Zhongxing Temple, faced off until evening, and each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Xinting; the rebels drew up at Zhongxing Temple, and the two sides faced each other until evening before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 是夜，仲禮入粲營部分眾軍，旦日將戰，諸將各有據守。

translations.literal: That night Zhongli entered Can's camp to array the armies; at dawn they would fight, and each general had his assigned defense.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhongli entered Can's camp to deploy the forces; at dawn battle would be joined, and each commander was assigned his position.

sentences.zh: 令粲頓青塘，當石頭中路。

translations.literal: Can was ordered to halt at Qingtang, blocking the central road to Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Can was assigned to hold Qingtang, blocking the central approach to Stone City.

sentences.zh: 粲慮柵壘未立，賊爭之，頗以為憚，謂仲禮曰：「下官才非禦侮，直欲以身徇國，節下善量其宜，不可致有虧喪。」

translations.literal: Can worried that the palisades and ramparts were not yet set; the rebels vied for the position and he was quite apprehensive. He said to Zhongli, "This subordinate's talent is not for repelling insult; I only wish to give my body in service to the state. Your Lordship, please weigh what is fitting well—do not let there be loss or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Can worried that the fortifications were not yet complete and that the rebels would contest the ground; he was deeply uneasy. He told Zhongli, "I am no match for the enemy in talent—I only mean to give my life for the realm. Your Lordship must judge what is prudent; we must not suffer needless loss.

sentences.zh: 仲禮曰：「青塘立營，迫近淮渚，欲以糧儲船乘盡就迫之。

translations.literal: Zhongli said, "To establish a camp at Qingtang, pressing close to the Huai sandbars, is meant to drive all grain stores and boats to press upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli replied, "Establishing a camp at Qingtang, close to the Huai sandbars, will let us press all our grain stores and shipping against the enemy there.

sentences.zh: 此事大，非兄不可。

translations.literal: This matter is great; it cannot be done without Elder Brother.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave undertaking—it cannot succeed without you, Elder Brother.

sentences.zh: 若疑兵少，當更差軍相助。」

translations.literal: If you doubt the troops are few, additional troops should be dispatched to assist."
translations.idiomatic: If you think our force is too small, send more troops to help."

sentences.zh: 粲帥所部水陸俱進。

translations.literal: Can led his command by land and water together advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Can led his troops forward by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 時昏霧，軍人失道，比及青塘，夜已過半，壘柵至曉未合。

translations.literal: At the time there was dusk fog; the soldiers lost the road. By the time they reached Qingtang, more than half the night had passed, and the ramparts and palisades were not joined even by dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Evening fog descended and the troops lost their way. By the time they reached Qingtang more than half the night was gone, and the ramparts were still incomplete at dawn.

sentences.zh: 景登禪靈寺門，望粲營未立，便率銳卒來攻。

translations.literal: Jing mounted the gate of Chanling Temple, saw Can's camp not yet established, and at once led crack troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jing climbed to the gate of Chanling Temple, saw that Can's camp was not yet ready, and immediately led elite troops to the attack.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，乘勝入營，左右高馮牽粲避賊，粲不動，兵死略盡，遂見害。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; pressing the victory they entered the camp. Those at Can's sides, Gao and Feng, pulled Can to avoid the rebels; Can did not move. The soldiers died almost to the last man, and he was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: The army was routed and the enemy stormed the camp. Gao and Feng at Can's side tried to pull him away from the rebels, but he would not budge. His men were slaughtered almost to a man, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 粲子尼及三弟助、警、構、從弟昂皆戰死，親戚死者數百人。

translations.literal: Can's son Ni and three younger brothers Zhu, Jing, and Gou, and his cousin Ang, all died in battle; relatives who died numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Can's son Ni, his three younger brothers Zhu, Jing, and Gou, and his cousin Ang all fell in battle; several hundred kinsmen died with them.

sentences.zh: 賊傳粲首闕下，以示城內。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Can's head beneath the palace gate tower to display it inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Can's head to the palace gate and displayed it to the city.

sentences.zh: 簡文聞之流涕，謂御史中丞蕭愷曰：「社稷所寄，唯在韋公，如何不幸，先死行陣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen heard of it he wept and said to the Censor-in-Chief Xiao Kai, "The trust of the altars of soil and grain rested only in Lord Wei—how unlucky that he should die first in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen heard the news he wept and said to Censor-in-Chief Xiao Kai, "The fate of the realm rested on Lord Wei alone—how cruel that he should fall first on the field.

sentences.zh: 詔贈護軍將軍。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 元帝平侯景，追諡忠貞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan suppressed Hou Jing, he posthumously enfeoffed him with the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan suppressed Hou Jing, he granted Can the posthumous title Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 子諒，以學業為陳始興王叔陵所引，為中錄事參軍兼記室。

translations.literal: His son Liang, for his learning was taken up by Chen Prince of Shixing Shuling, and served as Central Recording Affairs Aide while also holding Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang, noted for scholarship, was taken up by Prince Shuling of Shixing and served as central recording affairs aide and secretariat officer.

sentences.zh: 叔陵敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Shuling was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling fell, Liang was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 放弟正。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zheng was released.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zheng was released from custody.

sentences.zh: 正字敬直，位襄陵太守。

translations.literal: Zheng, style Jingzhi, held the post of Governor of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, courtesy name Jingzhi, served as governor of Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，正與東海王僧孺善，及僧孺為吏部郎，參掌大選，賓友故人莫不傾意，正獨澹然。

translations.literal: At first Zheng was on good terms with Wang Sengru of Donghai; when Sengru became Director of the Ministry of Personnel and jointly managed the great selection, guests, friends, and old acquaintances all exerted themselves to please him—Zheng alone remained detached.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had been close to Wang Sengru of Donghai. When Sengru became director of the Ministry of Personnel and shared control of high appointments, friends and acquaintances all courted him eagerly—Zheng alone remained aloof.

sentences.zh: 及僧孺擯廢，正復篤素分，有踰曩日，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: When Sengru was dismissed and disgraced, Zheng again honored their old bond, even more than in former days; commentators praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengru was stripped of office and disgraced, Zheng renewed their old friendship with even greater constancy than before, and observers praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒于給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Attendant at the Gates of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as attendant at the gates of the yellow gate in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子載。

translations.literal: His son was Zai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zai.

sentences.zh: 載字德基，少聰慧，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Zai, style Deji, from youth was clever and intelligent, with steadfast purpose and love of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zai, courtesy name Deji, was clever from boyhood, devoted in purpose and eager to learn.

sentences.zh: 年十二，隨叔父棱見沛國劉顯，顯問漢書十事，載隨問應無疑滯。

translations.literal: At age twelve, following his uncle Leng he visited Liu Xian of Pei; Xian asked ten matters from the Book of Han, and Zai answered each question as it came without hesitation or delay.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he accompanied his uncle Leng to visit Liu Xian of Pei. Xian posed ten questions on the Book of Han, and Zai answered each without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉文史，沈敏有器局。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged broadly through literature and history, was deep and quick-witted, and had capacity and breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered literature and history, was keen-minded and steady, and showed breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was a Secretary in the Three Dukes Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as secretary in the three dukes bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝承制，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Hou Jing, Emperor Yuan, acting on imperial authority, appointed him Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan, exercising provisional authority, appointed him palace secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋為尋陽太守，隨都督王僧辯東討侯景。

translations.literal: Soon he became Governor of Xunyang and followed the commander-in-chief Wang Sengbian east to suppress Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Xunyang and followed Commander Wang Sengbian east to suppress Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，歷位琅邪、義興太守。

translations.literal: When Jing was suppressed, he successively held the posts of Governor of Langye and Governor of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he served in succession as governor of Langye and governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝誅王僧辯，乃遣周文育襲載，載嬰城自守。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi executed Wang Sengbian, he sent Zhou Wenyue to surprise Zai; Zai closed the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen killed Wang Sengbian, he sent Zhou Wenyue to attack Zai, who shut the city gates and defended it.

sentences.zh: 載所屬縣卒，並陳武舊兵，多善用弩，載收得數十人，系以長鎖，令所親監之，使射文育軍。

translations.literal: The district soldiers under Zai were all old troops of Chen Wu and many were skilled with crossbows; Zai gathered several dozen men, bound them with long chains, had those close to him supervise them, and made them shoot at Wenyue's army.
translations.idiomatic: The district troops under Zai were veterans of Emperor Wu's old army and many were expert crossbowmen. Zai collected several dozen of them, chained them together, placed them under trusted overseers, and set them to shoot at Wenyue's forces.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「十發不兩中者死。」

translations.literal: He stipulated, "Whoever does not hit twice in ten shots dies.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that any man who failed to score two hits in ten shots would be put to death.

sentences.zh: 每發輒中，所中皆斃，相持數旬。

translations.literal: Each shot hit; those struck all died. They faced off for several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Every shot found its mark and every man struck fell dead. The siege dragged on for weeks.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝聞文育軍不利，以書喻載以誅王僧辯意，並奉梁敬帝敕，敕載解兵。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi, hearing Wenyue's army was faring ill, sent a letter explaining to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to disband his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wenyue's campaign was going badly, Emperor Wu of Chen wrote to Zai explaining why he had killed Wang Sengbian and enclosed an edict from Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to lay down arms.

sentences.zh: 載得書，乃以眾降。

translations.literal: When Zai received the letter, he then surrendered with his host.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the letter, Zai surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝引載恒置左右，與之謀議。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi kept Zai constantly at his side and consulted with him in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu kept Zai constantly at his side and consulted him on policy.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等引齊軍濟江，據石頭城，帝問計於載。

translations.literal: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others brought Qi troops across the river and held Stone City; the Emperor asked Zai's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others brought Northern Qi troops across the Yangzi and seized Stone City; the emperor asked Zai for counsel.

sentences.zh: 載曰：「齊軍若分兵先據三吳之路，略地東境，則時事去矣。

translations.literal: Zai said, "If the Qi army divides its forces first to hold the roads of the Three Wu and plunder the eastern territories, then the times will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said, "If the Qi army splits up first to seize the routes into the Three Wu and ravage the eastern provinces, all will be lost.

sentences.zh: 今可急於淮南即侯景故壘築城，以通東道轉輸，別令輕兵絕其糧運，使進無所虜，退無所資，則齊將之首，旬日可致。」

translations.literal: Now one should urgently build a city at the old ramparts of Hou Jing on the Huai River to open an eastern supply route, and separately send light troops to cut their grain transport—then with advance they will have nothing to plunder and with retreat nothing to sustain them, and the heads of the Qi generals can be obtained within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: We should quickly fortify Hou Jing's old camp on the Huai to open an eastern supply line, and send light troops to sever their grain convoys. Cut off plunder on the advance and supplies on the retreat, and the Qi commanders' heads can be taken within ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，司徒王僧辯以為戶曹屬。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was suppressed, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian made him an aide in the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian appointed him aide in the household bureau.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to palace secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝在南徐州，鼎望氣知其當王，遂寄孥焉。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi was at Southern Xu Province, Ding read the qi and knew he would become king; he therefore sent his wife and children to lodge there.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu of Chen was still at Southern Xu Province, Ding read the signs of fate and knew he would become emperor; he sent his family to settle there.

sentences.zh: 因謂陳武帝曰：「明年有大臣誅死，後四歲，梁其代終。

translations.literal: He therefore said to Chen Wudi, "Next year a great minister will be executed; four years later the Liang will reach its end.
translations.idiomatic: He told Emperor Wu, "Next year a great minister will be put to death; four years from now the Liang dynasty will end.

sentences.zh: 天之歷數，當歸舜後。
