translations.literal: Heaven's succession should return to the line of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate will pass to the house of Shun.

sentences.zh: 昔周滅殷氏，封媯汭于宛丘，其裔子孫，因為陳氏。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zhou destroyed the Yin, it enfeoffed Gui Ruo at Wanchen; his descendants and offspring therefore became the house of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou overthrew the Yin, it enfeoffed Gui Ruo at Wanchen; his descendants became the house of Chen.

sentences.zh: 僕觀明公，天縱神武，繼絕統者無乃是乎。」

translations.literal: Your servant observes that Your Lordship is heaven-endowed and divinely martial—the one who restores a broken succession is surely none other than you.
translations.idiomatic: I see in Your Lordship heaven's gift and divine martial prowess—you are surely the one destined to restore a fallen line.

sentences.zh: 武帝陰有圖僧辯意，聞其言大喜，因而定策。

translations.literal: Wudi secretly already had a design against Sengbian; hearing these words he was greatly pleased and thereby settled his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already harbored secret designs against Sengbian; hearing this he was overjoyed and fixed his resolve.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Ding was appointed Attendant at the Gates of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Ding was appointed attendant at the gates of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 太建中，以廷尉卿為聘周使，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, as Minister of Justice he served as envoy on an embassy to Northern Zhou and was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During Taijian he served as minister of justice on an embassy to Northern Zhou and was also made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後為太府卿。

translations.literal: Later he became Minister of the Palace Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He later became minister of the palace storehouses.

sentences.zh: 至德初，鼎盡貨田宅，寓居僧寺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, Ding sold off all his fields and houses and lodged in a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhide era Ding sold all his land and property and moved into a monastery.

sentences.zh: 友人大匠卿毛彪問其故，答曰：「江東王氣，盡於此矣。

translations.literal: His friend Mao Biao, Master of Works, asked the reason; he answered, "The royal qi of the Jiangdong is exhausted here.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Mao Biao, master of works, asked why; he replied, "The imperial fortune of the Jiangdong is spent.

sentences.zh: 吾與爾當葬長安，期運將及，故破產爾。」

translations.literal: You and I will be buried in Chang'an—the appointed time is near, so I am ruining my estate for it."
translations.idiomatic: You and I will be buried in Chang'an—the fated hour is near, so I am disposing of my property now."

sentences.zh: 初，鼎之聘周也，嘗遇隋文帝，謂曰：「觀公容貌，不久必大貴，貴則天下一家。

translations.literal: At first, when Ding went on the embassy to Zhou, he once met Emperor Wen of Sui and said to him, "Observing Your Lordship's countenance, before long you will surely attain great nobility; when noble, the realm will become one family.
translations.idiomatic: On his embassy to Zhou he once met Emperor Wen of Sui and told him, "Judging by your bearing, you will soon rise to supreme rank—and when you do, the realm will be united under one house.

sentences.zh: 歲一周天，老夫當委質，願深自愛。」

translations.literal: In one cycle of heaven I, your old servant, will offer my allegiance; please deeply cherish yourself.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven completes one full cycle I shall submit to you—until then, take good care of yourself.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，驛召入京，授上儀同三司，待遇甚厚，每公宴，鼎恒預焉。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he was summoned post-haste to the capital and appointed Senior Master of Ceremonies of the Third Rank, with treatment very generous; at every public banquet Ding was always present.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he was summoned urgently to the capital, made senior master of ceremonies of the third rank, and treated with great honor; he was always present at state banquets.

sentences.zh: 性簡貴，雖為亡國之臣，未嘗俯仰當世。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and noble; though a subject of a fallen state, he never bowed and scraped before the age.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and proud by nature, he never truckled to the powers of the day, though he was a minister of a conquered realm.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書韋世康兄弟顯貴，隋文帝從容謂鼎曰：「世康與公遠近？」

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Personnel Wei Shikang and his brothers were conspicuously honored; Emperor Wen of Sui said at leisure to Ding, "How near or far is Shikang to you in kinship?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shikang, minister of personnel, and his brothers were then in high favor. Emperor Wen asked Ding casually, "How closely are you related to Shikang?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣宗族南徙，昭穆非臣所知。」

translations.literal: He answered, "My clan migrated south; the lineages of the ancestral temple are not what your servant knows."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My branch of the clan moved south long ago—the ancestral tables are beyond my knowledge."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿百代卿族，豈忘本也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "You are a ministerial clan for a hundred generations—how can you forget your roots?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your house has produced ministers for a hundred generations—surely you have not forgotten your origins."

sentences.zh: 命官給酒肴，遣世康請鼎還杜陵。

translations.literal: He ordered officials to supply wine and viands and sent Shikang to invite Ding to return to Dulang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered wine and food provided and sent Shikang to bring Ding home to Dulang.

sentences.zh: 鼎乃自楚太傅孟以下二十餘世，並考論昭穆，作韋氏譜七卷示之，歡飲十餘日乃還。

translations.literal: Ding then traced more than twenty generations from Meng, Grand Tutor of Chu, downward, examined and discussed the ancestral lines, and composed a seven-scroll Genealogy of the Wei Clan to show them; they feasted for more than ten days before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ding then traced more than twenty generations from Meng, grand tutor of Chu, downward, worked out the ancestral lines, and produced a seven-scroll genealogy of the Wei clan for them; they feasted together for more than ten days before he returned.

sentences.zh: 時蘭陵公主寡，上為之求夫，選親衛柳述及蕭瑒等以示鼎，鼎曰：「瑒當封侯，而無貴妻之相；

translations.literal: At the time Princess of Lanling was widowed; the Emperor sought a husband for her, selected the imperial guard Liu Shu and Xiao Yang among others to show Ding. Ding said, "Yang will be enfeoffed as marquis, but he has not the countenance of a noble wife;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling was then a widow, and the emperor sought a husband for her. He picked out the imperial guardsman Liu Shu and Xiao Yang among others and showed them to Ding. Ding said, "Yang will receive a marquisate, but he lacks the bearing of a consort to rank;

sentences.zh: 述亦通顯，而守位不終。」

translations.literal: Shu too will reach eminence, but he will not hold rank to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Shu will also rise high, but he will not keep his position to the end.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「位由我爾。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Rank is mine to give."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rank is mine to bestow."

sentences.zh: 遂以主降述。

translations.literal: He thereupon gave the princess in marriage to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave the princess to Shu in marriage.

sentences.zh: 上又問鼎，諸兒誰為嗣位。

translations.literal: The Emperor again asked Ding which of his sons would succeed to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked Ding which of his sons would inherit the throne.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「至尊皇后所最愛者，當與之，非臣敢預知也。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Whomever the August One and the Empress most favor—that one will receive it; it is not for your servant to presume to know beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Whoever Your Majesty and the empress favor most will receive it—that is not for me to foretell.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「不肯顯言乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "You refuse to speak plainly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "So you won't say it outright?"

sentences.zh: 開皇十三年，除光州刺史，以仁義教導，務弘清靜。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Guang Province; with benevolence and righteousness he instructed the people and devoted himself to promoting clarity and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang he was appointed governor of Guang Province, where he governed with benevolence and righteousness and strove to keep the realm tranquil and clear.

sentences.zh: 州中有土豪，外修邊幅，而內行不軌，常為劫盜。

translations.literal: In the province there was a local strongman who outwardly cultivated propriety but inwardly did not keep to the Way, and often acted as bandit and robber.
translations.idiomatic: In the province lived a local magnate who kept up a respectable front while breaking the law within, and often led raids and robberies.

sentences.zh: 鼎于都會時謂之曰：「卿是好人，那忽作賊。」

translations.literal: At a provincial assembly Ding said to him, "You are a good man—why suddenly act as a bandit?
translations.idiomatic: At a provincial gathering Ding said to him, "You are an upright man—why turn bandit?

sentences.zh: 因條其徒黨奸謀逗遛，其人驚懼，即自首伏。

translations.literal: He then listed the wicked plots and delays of his gang; the man was alarmed and afraid and at once confessed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out the conspiracies and evasions of the man's followers; terrified, the man confessed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又有人客遊，通主家之妾，及其還去，妾盜珍物，於夜逃亡，尋於草中為人所殺。

translations.literal: Again there was a traveling guest who had an affair with his host's concubine; when he was about to leave, the concubine stole precious objects and fled by night, and soon afterward was killed by someone in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Another case involved a traveling guest who had taken the master's concubine as lover; when he was leaving, the concubine stole valuables and fled by night, and was soon found slain in the underbrush.

sentences.zh: 主家知客與妾通，因告客殺之。

translations.literal: The master's household knew the guest had been intimate with the concubine and therefore reported that the guest had killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The household knew of the affair and accused the guest of murder.

sentences.zh: 縣司鞫問，具得奸狀，因斷客死。

translations.literal: The county office interrogated him and fully obtained the facts of the illicit affair; they therefore sentenced the guest to death.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate examined the case, established the affair, and sentenced the guest to death.

sentences.zh: 獄成，上於鼎，鼎覽之，曰：「此客實奸，而不殺也。

translations.literal: When the case was complete it was submitted to Ding; Ding read it and said, "This guest was indeed licentious, but he did not kill her.
translations.idiomatic: When the file reached Ding he read it and said, "The guest was indeed guilty of adultery, but he did not kill her.

sentences.zh: 乃某寺僧眩妾盜物，令奴殺之，贓在某處。」

translations.literal: It was a monk of a certain temple who bewitched the concubine to steal objects; he had a slave kill her, and the stolen goods are at a certain place.
translations.idiomatic: A monk at a certain temple bewitched the concubine into stealing the goods and had a servant kill her; the loot is hidden at such-and-such a place.

sentences.zh: 即放此客，遣人掩僧，並獲贓物。

translations.literal: He at once released this guest, sent men to seize the monk, and recovered the stolen goods as well.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately freed the guest, sent men to arrest the monk, and recovered the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 自是部內肅然，咸稱其神，道無拾遺。

translations.literal: From this the district was orderly; all called him divine, and nothing was picked up on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the district was orderly; all called him uncanny in judgment, and lost property went unclaimed on the roads.

sentences.zh: 尋追入京，頃之，而卒于長安，年七十九。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to the capital; before long he died at Chang'an, age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital and died at Chang'an shortly afterward, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 正弟棱。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother was Leng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother was Leng.

sentences.zh: 棱字威直，性恬素，以書史為業，博物強記，當世士咸就質疑。

translations.literal: Leng, style Weizhi, was by nature quiet and plain; he made books and histories his profession, was broadly learned with a strong memory, and men of the age all came to him with questions.
translations.idiomatic: Leng, courtesy name Weizhi, was quiet and plain by nature; he devoted himself to books and history, was widely learned with a prodigious memory, and scholars of the day came to him for answers.

sentences.zh: 位終光祿卿。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 著漢書續訓三卷。

translations.literal: He authored Continued Instruction on the Book of Han in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Continued Instruction on the Book of Han in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 棱弟黯。

translations.literal: Leng's younger brother was An.
translations.idiomatic: Leng's younger brother was An.

sentences.zh: 黯字務直，性強正，少習經史，位太府卿。

translations.literal: An, style Wuzhi, was by nature forceful and upright; from youth he studied the classics and histories, and held the post of Minister of the Palace Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: An, courtesy name Wuzhi, was forceful and upright by nature; he studied the classics and histories from youth and served as minister of the palace storehouses.

sentences.zh: 侯景濟江，黯屯六門，尋改為都督城西面諸軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the river, An encamped at the Six Gates; soon he was changed to commander of all armies on the western face of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, An encamped at the Six Gates; he was soon made commander of all forces on the city's western face.

sentences.zh: 時景於城外起東西二土山，城內亦應之，簡文親自負土，哀太子以下，躬執畚鍤。

translations.literal: At the time Jing raised eastern and western earthen hills outside the city; inside the city they responded in kind, and Emperor Jianwen personally carried earth, while from the Crown Prince of Ai downward all personally wielded spades and baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing raised earthen siege mounds east and west outside the walls; the defenders built counter-mounds within, and Emperor Jianwen himself carried earth while the crown prince and all below him wielded spades and baskets.

sentences.zh: 黯守西土山，晝夜苦戰。

translations.literal: An defended the western earthen hill, fighting bitterly day and night.
translations.idiomatic: An held the western mound and fought bitterly day and night.

sentences.zh: 以功授輕車將軍，加持節，卒於城內。

translations.literal: For merit he was awarded General of Light Chariots and additionally given the staff of command; he died inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made general of light chariots with the staff of command and died within the city.

sentences.zh: 初，黯為太僕卿，而兄子粲為左衛率，黯以故常怏怏，謂人曰：「韋粲已落驊騮前，朝廷是能用才不？」

translations.literal: At first, when An was Minister of the Imperial Stud and his elder brother's son Can was Commander of the Left Guard, An was often discontent on that account and said to people, "Wei Can has already fallen before the bay horse—can the court truly employ talent or not?
translations.idiomatic: When An was minister of the imperial stud and his nephew Can was commander of the left guard, An was often resentful and said, "Wei Can has already fallen before the bay stallion—is this court capable of using real talent?

sentences.zh: 識者頗以此窺之。

translations.literal: Those who understood thereby gained a glimpse of his character.
translations.idiomatic: Observers took this as a measure of his character.

sentences.zh: 裴邃字深明，河東聞喜人，魏冀州刺史徽之後也。

translations.literal: Pei Sui, style Shenming, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong, a descendant of Pei Hui, Governor of Ji Province of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui, courtesy name Shenming, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong and a descendant of Pei Hui, governor of Ji Province under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖壽孫，寓居壽陽，為宋武帝前軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shousun lived as a sojourner at Shouyang and served as Chief Aide to the Vanguard Army of Emperor Wu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shousun settled at Shouyang and served as chief aide to the vanguard army of Emperor Wu of Song.

sentences.zh: 父仲穆，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhongmu was General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongmu was general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 邃十歲能屬文，善左氏春秋。

translations.literal: Sui at age ten could compose prose and was skilled in the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Sui could already compose prose and was adept in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 齊東昏踐阼，始安王蕭遙光為揚州刺史，引邃為參軍。

translations.literal: When Dong Hun of Qi ascended the throne, Prince Xiaoguang of Shian was Governor of Yang Province and took Sui as Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun of Qi came to the throne, Prince Xiaoguang of Shian, governor of Yang Province, took Sui on as aide.

sentences.zh: 遙光敗，邃還壽陽，會刺史裴叔業以壽陽降魏，邃遂隨眾北徙。

translations.literal: When Xiaoguang was defeated, Sui returned to Shouyang; it happened that the Governor Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei, and Sui therefore followed the multitude north in migration.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoguang fell, Sui returned to Shouyang; Governor Pei Shuye surrendered the city to Wei, and Sui moved north with the population.

sentences.zh: 魏宣武帝雅重之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu of Wei honored him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu of Wei held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He served Wei as Grand Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Wei as grand administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏遣王肅鎮壽陽，邃固求隨肅，密圖南歸。

translations.literal: Wei dispatched Wang Su to garrison Shouyang; Sui insistently asked to follow Su, secretly planning to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Wang Su to garrison Shouyang; Sui pressed hard to join him, secretly plotting to defect south.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，自拔南還，除後軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, he extricated himself and returned south, and was appointed Consultant to the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang Tianjian era he made his own escape south and was made consultant to the rear army.

sentences.zh: 邃求邊境自效，以為廬江太守。

translations.literal: Sui requested to prove himself on the frontier, and was made Grand Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui asked to serve on the border and was appointed grand administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，征邵陽洲，魏人為長橋斷淮以濟，邃築壘逼橋，每戰輒克，於是密作沒突艦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he attacked Shaoyang Isle; the Wei people built a long bridge to block the Huai for crossing; Sui built fortifications pressing the bridge, winning every battle; thereupon he secretly constructed assault vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned against Shaoyang Isle. The Wei built a long pontoon bridge across the Huai; Sui raised fortifications to press the bridge and won every clash, then secretly built assault vessels.

sentences.zh: 會甚雨，淮水暴溢，邃乘艦徑造橋側，進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy rain fell and the Huai waters surged; Sui took his vessels straight to the bridge's side, advanced and attacked, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains swelled the Huai, and Sui drove his vessels straight to the bridge, attacked, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 以功封夷陵縣子。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiling County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was ennobled as viscount of Yiling County.

sentences.zh: 遷廣陵太守，與鄉人共入魏武廟，因論帝王功業。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Administrator of Guangling; together with a fellow townsman he entered the temple of Emperor Wu of Wei, and thereupon discussed the achievements of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to grand administrator of Guangling, he entered the shrine of Cao Cao with a fellow townsman and fell to discussing the founding deeds of rulers.

sentences.zh: 其妻甥王篆之密啟梁武帝云：「裴邃多大言，有不臣跡。」

translations.literal: His wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi secretly reported to Emperor Wu of Liang, saying: "Pei Sui speaks grandly of many things and shows signs of disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: His wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi secretly informed Emperor Wu, "Pei Sui talks too boldly and shows signs of treasonous ambition."

sentences.zh: 由是左遷始安太守。

translations.literal: On this account he was demoted and transferred to Grand Administrator of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to grand administrator of Shian.

sentences.zh: 邃志立功邊陲，不願閑遠，乃致書于呂僧珍曰：「昔阮咸、顏延有二始之歎，吾才不逮古人，今為三始，非其願也，將如之何！」

translations.literal: Sui aspired to establish merit on the frontier and did not wish for a distant idle post; he therefore wrote to Lu Sengzhen, saying: "In the past Ruan Xian and Yan Yan had the lament of two starts; my talent does not reach the ancients, yet now I have a third start—this is not what I wished; what am I to do!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui meant to win glory on the frontier and had no wish for a sleepy remote post; he wrote to Lu Sengzhen, "Ruan Xian and Yan Yan each lamented being sent to Shian twice. I am no match for those men, yet this is my third exile there—it is not what I wanted. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 後為竟陵太守，開置屯田，公私便之。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Administrator of Jingling, opened and established military colonies, and both public and private interests benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made grand administrator of Jingling, where he opened military colonies to the benefit of the region.

sentences.zh: 再遷西戎校尉、北梁秦二州刺史，復開創屯田數千頓，倉廩盈實，省息邊運，人吏獲安。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Colonel of the Western Barbarians and Governor of the two provinces of Northern Liang and Qin; again he opened military colonies numbering several thousand dun, granaries were full and solid, border transport was saved, and people and officials found peace.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred again as colonel of the western barbarians and governor of Northern Liang and Qin provinces, he once more established thousands of military colonies, filling the granaries, easing frontier supply lines, and bringing stability to people and officials alike.

sentences.zh: 乃相率餉絹千餘匹，邃從容曰：「汝等不應爾，吾又不可逆。」

translations.literal: Thereupon they jointly presented more than a thousand bolts of silk as tribute; Sui calmly said: "You ought not to act thus; yet I also cannot refuse outright."
translations.idiomatic: The people together offered more than a thousand bolts of silk in gratitude; Sui said calmly, "You should not do this—but neither can I simply turn you away."

sentences.zh: 納其二匹而已。

translations.literal: He accepted only two bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He took only two bolts.

sentences.zh: 入為大匠卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as minister of construction.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，義州刺史文僧明以州入魏，魏軍來援，以邃為信武將軍，督眾軍討焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, Wen Shengming, Governor of Yi Province, brought the province into Wei; Wei armies came to assist, and Sui was made General of Trustworthy Martiality to command the armies in punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Putong the governor of Yi Province, Wen Shengming, defected to Wei with his province. Wei sent reinforcements, and Sui was made general of trustworthy martiality to lead the punitive force.

sentences.zh: 邃深入魏境，出其不意。

translations.literal: Sui penetrated deep into Wei territory, taking them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Sui marched deep into Wei territory and struck before they were prepared.

sentences.zh: 魏所署義州刺史封壽據檀公峴，邃擊破之，遂圍其城。

translations.literal: Feng Shou, whom Wei had appointed Governor of Yi Province, held Tanggong Xian; Sui defeated him and thereupon besieged his city.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shou, Wei's appointee as governor of Yi Province, held Tanggong Pass; Sui routed him and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 壽請降，義州平。

translations.literal: Shou requested surrender; Yi Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shou surrendered and Yi Province was restored.

sentences.zh: 除豫州刺史，加督，鎮合肥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Yu Province, with added command, and garrisoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Yu Province with broad authority and stationed at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 四年，大軍北侵，以邃督征討諸軍事，先襲壽陽，攻其郛，斬門而入，一日戰九合，為後軍蔡秀成失道不至，邃以援絕拔還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the great army invaded north; Sui was made Commander of All Punitive and Expeditionary Affairs; he first struck Shouyang, attacked its outer wall, cut through the gate and entered, in one day fought nine engagements; because the rear army under Cai Xiucheng lost the way and did not arrive, Sui, with reinforcements cut off, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the main army marched north. Sui directed the expedition, first raiding Shouyang, breaking through the outer defenses in a day of nine pitched battles—but reinforcements under Cai Xiucheng lost their way, and with support cut off Sui had to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 於是邃復整兵，收集士卒，令諸將各以服色相別。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sui again reorganized his troops, gathered soldiers, and ordered the various generals each to distinguish themselves by color of dress.
translations.idiomatic: Sui regrouped, rallied his troops, and had each commander mark his men by the color of their garments.

sentences.zh: 邃自為黃袍騎，先攻拔狄丘、甓城、黎漿，又屠安成、馬頭、沙陵等戍。

translations.literal: Sui himself rode in a yellow robe, first attacked and captured Diqiu, Bicheng, and Lijiang, and furthermore stormed the garrisons of Ancheng, Matou, Shaling, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing a yellow robe and riding at the head, Sui took Diqiu, Bicheng, and Lijiang, then stormed the garrisons at Ancheng, Matou, Shaling, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 明年，略地至汝、潁間，所在回應。

translations.literal: The next year, he seized territory reaching between Ru and Ying; everywhere people responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he swept the country between the Ru and Ying rivers, and local populations rallied to him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 魏壽陽守將長孫承業、河間王元琛出城挑戰，邃臨淮歎曰：「今日不破河間，方為謝玄所笑。」

translations.literal: The Wei garrison commanders of Shouyang, Zhangsun Chengye and Prince Yuan Chen of Hejian, came out of the city to challenge battle; Sui, facing the Huai, sighed and said: "If today I do not defeat Prince Hejian, I shall yet be laughed at by Xie Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang's Wei defenders, Zhangsun Chengye and Prince Yuan Chen of Hejian, rode out to challenge him. Sui gazed across the Huai and said, "If I fail to break Prince Hejian today, Xie Xuan will laugh at me from the grave."

sentences.zh: 乃為四甄以待之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he formed four wings to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged his forces in four wings to receive them.

sentences.zh: 令直閣將軍李祖憐偽遁以引承業，承業等悉眾追之，四甄競發，魏眾大敗，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: He ordered Direct Attendant General Li Zulin to feign retreat and lure Chengye; Chengye and the others pursued with their full forces; the four wings competed to strike; the Wei host was utterly defeated, with more than ten thousand heads severed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Li Zulin to feign flight and draw Chengye out; the Wei force pursued in full strength, all four wings closed in at once, and the enemy was shattered with more than ten thousand killed.

sentences.zh: 承業奔走，閉門不敢復出。

translations.literal: Chengye fled in haste, closed the gates, and did not dare come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye fled back inside and shut the gates, daring not sally forth again.

sentences.zh: 在軍疾篤，命眾軍守備，送喪還合肥。

translations.literal: While in camp his illness grew grave; he ordered the armies to maintain defenses and had his coffin sent back to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened in camp; he ordered the army to hold its positions and had his body sent back to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈侍中、左衛將軍，進爵為侯，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; posthumously awarded Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard, advanced in rank to Marquis, posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly afterward and was posthumously made attendant-in-ordinary and general of the left guard, raised to marquis with the posthumous name Lie ("Fierce").

sentences.zh: 邃沈深有思略，為政寬明，能得士心，居身方正，有威重。

translations.literal: Sui was deep, steady, and possessed of strategic thought; in governance he was lenient and clear; he could win the hearts of officers; in personal conduct he was upright, with authority and weight.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was deep-thinking and far-seeing, lenient yet clear in government, able to win the loyalty of his officers; upright in bearing, he carried real authority.

sentences.zh: 將吏憚之，少敢犯法。

translations.literal: Generals and clerks feared him and few dared violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders and clerks feared him, and few dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 及卒，淮、肥間莫不流涕，以為邃不死，當大辟土宇。

translations.literal: When he died, between the Huai and Fei none did not shed tears, thinking that had Sui not died, he would have greatly expanded the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the region between the Huai and Fei wept as one; many believed that had Sui lived, he would have greatly expanded Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 子之禮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhili succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhili inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 之禮字子義，美容儀，能言玄理。

translations.literal: Zhili, style Ziyi, had handsome appearance and could discourse on abstruse principles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili, courtesy name Ziyi, was handsome in bearing and skilled in philosophical discourse.

sentences.zh: 為西豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Western Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of western Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 母憂居喪，唯食麥飯。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he observed the mourning rites, eating only barley rice.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he ate only plain barley porridge.

sentences.zh: 邃廟在光宅寺西，堂宇弘敞，松柏鬱茂。

translations.literal: Sui's ancestral temple was west of Guangzhai Monastery; the hall was broad and spacious, pines and cypresses lush and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's shrine stood west of Guangzhai Monastery—its halls broad and its pines and cypresses thickly grown.

sentences.zh: 範雲廟在三橋，蓬蒿不翦。

translations.literal: Fan Yun's temple was at Sanqiao, weeds and artemisia uncut.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun's shrine at Sanqiao stood overgrown with weeds, untended.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝南郊，道經二廟，顧而歎曰：「范為已死，裴為更生。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang, proceeding to the southern suburb sacrifice, passed by the two temples, looked back and sighed: "Fan is already dead; Pei is as though born again."
translations.idiomatic: On his way to the southern suburb sacrifice, Emperor Wu passed both shrines and sighed, "Fan is dead, while Pei seems born anew."

sentences.zh: 大同初，都下旱蝗，四籬門外桐柏凋盡，唯邃墓犬牙不入，當時異之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, drought and locusts struck the capital; outside the Four Liy Gates the paulownia and cypress withered entirely; only Sui's tomb the locusts would not invade by a dog's tooth—people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: In early Datong a drought and locust plague withered every tree outside the capital gates—yet locusts would not touch Sui's tomb, to the wonder of all.

sentences.zh: 歷位黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Gentleman-attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman-attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 武帝設無遮會，舞象驚，排突陛衛，王公皆散，唯之禮與散騎常侍臧盾不動。

translations.literal: The Emperor set up a Boundless Charity Assembly; the dancing elephants were frightened, pushed and burst through the imperial guard; lords and princes all scattered; only Zhili and Regular Palace Attendant Zang Dun did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At a Buddhist assembly of universal charity, frightened dancing elephants broke through the imperial guard and princes fled in every direction—only Zhili and palace attendant Zang Dun stood firm.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，以之禮為壯勇將軍、北徐州刺史，盾兼中領軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired them; he made Zhili General of Robust Valor and Governor of Northern Xu Province, and Dun concurrently General of the Central Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and made Zhili general of robust valor and governor of northern Xu Province, while appointing Dun concurrent commander of the central army guard.

sentences.zh: 之禮卒於少府卿，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Zhili died while serving as Minister of the Lesser Treasury, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili died as minister of the lesser treasury and was posthumously named Zhuang ("Robust").

sentences.zh: 子政，承聖中位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zheng, during Chengsheng held the post of Supervising Gentleman-attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng served as supervising gentleman-attendant at the yellow gate during the Chengsheng reign.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he followed custom and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling he was taken to Chang'an like the rest of the captives.

sentences.zh: 之高字如山，邃兄中散大夫髦之子也。

translations.literal: Zhigao, style Rushan, was the son of Mao, Regular Master of Dispersal, elder brother of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao, courtesy name Rushan, was the son of Pei Mao, regular master of dispersal and elder brother of Sui.

sentences.zh: 頗讀書，少負意氣，常隨叔父邃征討，所在立功，甚為邃所器重，戎政咸以委焉。

translations.literal: He read books considerably; from youth he bore spirited resolve; he constantly followed his uncle Sui on campaigns of punishment and expedition, establishing merit wherever he went, and was greatly valued by Sui; military and civil affairs were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Well read and spirited from youth, he fought under his uncle Sui on campaign after campaign, winning distinction wherever he went and earning his full trust—Sui delegated all military and civil affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 壽陽之役，邃卒於軍所，之高隸夏侯夔平壽陽，仍除梁郡太守，封都城縣男。

translations.literal: In the Shouyang campaign, Sui died in the army camp; Zhigao served under Xiahou Gui in pacifying Shouyang, was then appointed Grand Administrator of Liang Commandery, and enfeoffed as Baron of Ducheng County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shouyang campaign Sui died in the field; Zhigao served under Xiahou Gui in taking the city, was made grand administrator of Liang Commandery, and ennobled as baron of Ducheng.

sentences.zh: 時魏汝陰來附，敕之高應接，仍除潁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Yin of Runan came over to allegiance from Wei; the emperor ordered Zhigao to receive him, and he was additionally appointed Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin of Runan defected from Wei, Zhigao was ordered to receive him and was made governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 父憂還都，起為光遠將軍，令討平陰陵盜，以為譙州刺史。

translations.literal: After mourning for his father he returned to the capital; he was recalled as General of Bright Distance and ordered to suppress and pacify the brigands of Yinling, and was made Governor of Qiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was made general of bright distance, ordered to crush brigands at Yinling, and appointed governor of Qiao Province.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，之高為西豫州刺史，率眾入援。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Zhigao was Governor of Western Yu Province and led troops to enter as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Zhigao, as governor of western Yu Province, marched in with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 南豫州刺史鄱陽嗣王范命之高總督江右援軍諸軍事，頓張公洲。

translations.literal: Fan, Prince of Poyang and successor king, Governor of Southern Yu Province, ordered Zhigao to oversee all military affairs of relief armies on the right bank of the Yangzi, encamping at Zhanggong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, Prince of Poyang and governor of southern Yu Province, put Zhigao in overall command of relief forces on the southern Yangzi and stationed him at Zhanggong Isle.

sentences.zh: 柳仲禮至橫江，之高遣船舸迎致仲禮，與韋粲等俱會青塘。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhongli reached Hengjiang, Zhigao dispatched boats to welcome and bring Zhongli, and together with Wei Can and others all assembled at Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli reached Hengjiang, Zhigao sent boats to fetch him and joined Wei Can and others at Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，之高還合肥，與鄱陽王範西上。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhigao returned to Hefei and with Prince Fan of Poyang marched westward.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell, Zhigao returned to Hefei and marched west with Prince Fan of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣召之，以為侍中、護軍將軍，到江陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sent summons for him; he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Protector General of the Army, and arrived at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan summoned him, made him attendant-in-ordinary and protector general of the army, and he went to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時之高第六弟之悌在侯景中。

translations.literal: At the time Zhigao's sixth younger brother Zhiti was among Hou Jing's followers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his sixth younger brother Zhiti was in Hou Jing's camp.

sentences.zh: 或傳之悌斬侯景，元帝使兼中書舍人黃羅漢報之高，之高竟無言，直云：「賊自殺賊，非之高所聞。」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Zhiti had beheaded Hou Jing; Emperor Yuan sent Concurrent Master of Writing Huang Luohan to inform Zhigao; Zhigao in the end said nothing further, simply saying: "The brigand killed the brigand—this is not something Zhigao has heard."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Zhiti had killed Hou Jing; Emperor Yuan sent Huang Luohan to tell Zhigao, who answered flatly, "One rebel killed another—that is nothing I have heard."

sentences.zh: 元帝深嗟其介直。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan deeply admired his stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan deeply admired his unbending integrity.

sentences.zh: 承制除特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: By imperial order on the way he was appointed Special Advance and Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial authority he was made special advancement holder and grand master with the gold seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 子畿，官至太子右衛率。

translations.literal: His son Ji reached the office of Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji rose to commandant of the crown prince's right guard.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，力戰死之。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling he fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 忌字無畏，少聰敏，有識量，頗涉史傳，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Ji, style Wuwei, from youth was bright and quick, possessed discernment and capacity, was broadly versed in histories and chronicles, and was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Wuwei, was clever and perceptive from youth, well read in history, and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，招集勇力，乃隨陳武帝征討。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he gathered brave and strong men, and then followed Emperor Wu of Chen on punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he mustered fighting men and followed the future Chen Emperor Wu on campaign.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝誅王僧辯，僧辯弟僧智舉兵據吳郡，陳武帝遣黃他攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen executed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's younger brother Sengzhi raised troops and seized Wu Commandery; Emperor Wu sent Huang Ta to attack but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Wu executed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's brother Sengzhi seized Wu commandery; Chen sent Huang Ta against him but failed to break the city.

sentences.zh: 命忌勒部下精兵，自錢唐直趣吳郡，夜至城下，鼓噪薄之。

translations.literal: He ordered Ji to lead his elite troops, from Qiantang straight toward Wu Commandery, arriving at the city walls by night, beating drums and shouting as they pressed close.
translations.idiomatic: Chen ordered Ji to lead his crack troops straight from Qiantang to Wu commandery; they reached the walls by night and attacked with drums and war cries.

sentences.zh: 僧智疑大軍至，輕舟奔杜龕，忌入據吳郡。

translations.literal: Sengzhi suspected a great army had arrived, fled light boat toward Du Kan, and Ji entered and seized Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhi, believing a main force had arrived, fled by boat toward Du Kan; Ji entered and held Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝嘉之，表授吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen praised him and memorialized to appoint him Grand Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu commended him and had him appointed grand administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 之橫字如嶽，少好賓遊，重氣俠，不事產業。

translations.literal: Zhiheng, style Ruyue, from youth loved hosting guests and travel, valued spirited chivalry, and did not attend to estate and property.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiheng, courtesy name Ruyue, loved entertaining and travel from youth, lived by the code of the bravo, and cared nothing for property.

sentences.zh: 之高以其縱誕，乃為狹被蔬食以激厲之。

translations.literal: Zhigao, because he was unrestrained and dissolute, therefore made narrow bedding and plain vegetable food to spur and discipline him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao, exasperated by his wild ways, gave him a thin blanket and plain food to shock him into reform.

sentences.zh: 之橫歎曰：「大丈夫富貴，必作百幅被。」

translations.literal: Zhiheng sighed and said: "When a great man grows rich and honored, he must surely make a quilt of a hundred layers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiheng sighed, "When a real man grows rich, he'll make himself a quilt of a hundred layers!"

sentences.zh: 遂與僮屬數百人於芍陂大營田墅，遂致殷積。

translations.literal: Thereupon with several hundred retainers and servants he at Shaobo greatly established farms and villas, and thus achieved abundant accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered several hundred servants and opened large estates at Shaobo Pond, soon amassing great wealth.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，聞而要之，以為河東王常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen of Liang, while in the Eastern Palace, heard of him and wanted him, appointing him Regular Attendant to the Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Jianwen was crown prince he sought Zhiheng out and made him regular attendant to the Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遷直合將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the direct guard.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，齊遣上党王高渙挾貞陽侯明攻東關。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Qi dispatched Prince Huan of Shangdang, escorting the Marquis of Zhenyang Ming, to attack Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei took Jiangling, Qi sent Prince Huan of Shangdang with the captive Marquis of Zhenyang to attack Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 晉安王承制，以之橫為徐州刺史，都督眾軍，出守蘄城。

translations.literal: Prince Jin'an, acting on imperial authority, made Zhiheng Governor of Xu Province, commander of all armies, to go out and garrison Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial authority, Prince Jin'an made Zhiheng governor of Xu Province, commander of all forces, and sent him to hold Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 之橫營壘未周，而齊軍大至，兵盡矢窮，遂於陣沒。

translations.literal: Zhiheng's fortifications were not yet complete when Qi armies arrived in force; troops exhausted and arrows spent, he thereupon perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Before his defenses were complete the Qi army arrived in force; out of men and arrows, he fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang ("Loyal and Robust").

sentences.zh: 子鳳寶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fengbao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengbao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 論曰：韋、裴少年勵操，俱以學尚自立，晚節驅馳，各著功於戎馬。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wei and Pei in youth encouraged their conduct, both establishing themselves through scholarly attainments; in their later years they rode forth in haste, each achieving merit on horseback in war.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In youth Wei and Pei disciplined their character and stood on learning; in later years they took to the saddle and each won distinction in war.

sentences.zh: 觀叡制勝之道，謂為魁梧之傑，然而形甚羸瘠，身不跨鞍，板輿指麾，隱如敵國，其器分有在，隆名豈虛得乎。

translations.literal: Observing Rui's way of securing victory, one would call him a towering hero; yet his form was exceedingly emaciated, his body never straddled the saddle—directing from a palanquin he seemed to confront a matching power; his capacity and allotment had their place—could his lofty name have been gained in vain?
translations.idiomatic: To watch Rui win battles is to see a commanding giant—yet he was painfully thin and never mounted a horse himself; from a hand carriage he directed armies as though facing an equal foe. Such gifts are rare; his towering reputation was hardly unearned.

sentences.zh: 邃自效邊疆，盛績克舉，其志不遂，良可悲夫。

translations.literal: Sui offered himself on the frontier, splendid achievements could be established—his ambition was not fulfilled; truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Sui gave his all on the frontier and piled victory upon victory—yet his ambition went unfulfilled, which is truly a pity.

sentences.zh: 二門子弟，各著名節，與梁終始，克荷隆構。

translations.literal: The sons and disciples of the two clans each achieved renowned integrity, shared Liang's fate from beginning to end, and were able to bear its lofty edifice.
translations.idiomatic: The younger generations of both houses won names for integrity, stood with Liang to the end, and shouldered its great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 「將門有將」，斯言豈曰妄乎。

translations.literal: "A general's house produces generals"—can this saying be called false?
translations.idiomatic: "A general's house breeds generals"—was that old saying ever untrue?
